definition_zh: 重要的；重大的；有影响力的
definition_en: having a great effect or value, and therefore deserving attention, care, or respect
core_image: 一张被反复推到桌子正中央的纸条，上面写着「这件事必须做」
scene: 开工前的班前会上，班长把一张写着安全要求的纸推到桌子正中，拍了拍。Safety, he stressed, is the important part.
sceneCN: 这里 important 是「重要的、重大的」（第 1 个义项：分量重、必须重视），句意是班长强调，安全才是最要紧的那一部分。画面里有班前会、一张被推到桌子中央的纸条和班长的手。

pos.zh: 形容词：重要的、重大的；有影响力的

derivatives.zh: 重要性、重要意义
重要地；重要的是
不重要的、无关紧要的

senses.title: Mattering a great deal
senses.definition: having a great effect or value, so that it deserves care and attention
senses.definitionCN: 影响或价值很大，因而值得用心对待
senses.example: Sleep is important for children who are still growing.
senses.exampleCN: 对还在长身高的孩子来说，睡眠很重要。
senses.why: This is the everyday sense: the thing carries weight and should not be ignored.
senses.whyCN: 这是最日常的义项：事情有分量，不能被忽略。

senses.title: Powerful or influential
senses.definition: having power or a high position in an organization or a field
senses.definitionCN: 在某个组织或领域里有权势、地位高
senses.example: She is an important figure in the city's music scene.
senses.exampleCN: 她在这个城市的音乐圈里是个有分量的人物。
senses.why: The weight spreads from the matter to the person who controls it, so the adjective describes people too.
senses.whyCN: 分量从事延伸到掌握事的人身上，于是这个形容词也能形容人。

senses.title: Solemn or self-asserting
senses.definition: used of a tone or manner that treats small things as very serious
senses.definitionCN: 形容一种把小事故意当成大事的语气或神态
senses.example: He gave an important nod before opening the envelope.
senses.exampleCN: 他煞有介事地点了点头，才拆开信封。
senses.why: Once a word for weight, it can also describe someone who plays at carrying weight.
senses.whyCN: 原本说分量的词，也能形容装出分量的人。

intro.en: Important is the adjective of import, which comes from the Latin verb for carrying something in.
intro.cn: important 是 import 的形容词形式，而 import 源自拉丁语中表示「搬进来」的动词。

items.en: Importare joined in, into, with portare, to carry, and meant to bring something in.
items.cn: 拉丁语 importare 把 in「进入」与 portare「搬运」组合起来，意为「把东西搬进来」。

items.en: Scholars used the verb for matters that carry meaning, so importare grew to mean to signify.
items.cn: 学者们用它来说「承载意义」的事，于是 importare 渐渐有了「意味着、关系重大」的意思。

items.en: French built the adjective important from the same stem, describing something of consequence.
items.cn: 法语由同一词干造出形容词 important，形容有后果、有关系的事物。

items.en: English adopted important in the sixteenth century, first in formal writing about serious matters.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪吸收 important，最初多见于谈论严肃事务的正式文章。

items.en: By the nineteenth century the adjective had spread into everyday speech and now covers people as well as things.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，这个形容词已进入日常口语，如今既能修饰事，也能修饰人。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the import family; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives with overlapping force.
note.cn: 形近组收 import 一族词；近义组收语义相近、强度不同的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of mattering.
entries.definitionCN: 名词形式，指「重要性」。

entries.definition: The adverb, used at the start of a sentence to add weight to a point.
entries.definitionCN: 副词形式，常置于句首为某一点加重分量。

entries.definition: The verb and noun about bringing in goods from other countries.
entries.definitionCN: 指「进口」的动词与名词，与 important 同源但侧重货物。

entries.definition: Large enough to be noticed and to affect a result.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「显著的、有意义的」，强调大到能被察觉并影响结果。

entries.definition: So important that something cannot work without it.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「必不可少的」，强调缺了就根本不行。

entries.definition: Deciding the outcome at one particular point.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「关键的」，指在某个节点上决定结果。

normalIntro.en: The hooks work on the carried-in root and on the phrases that English has fixed around the adjective.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子围绕「搬进来」的词根，以及英语中已经固定下来的搭配来展开。

normal.en: important shares its root with import, and both are about what gets carried into the centre.
normal.cn: important 与 import 同根，说的都是被搬到正中央的东西。

normal.en: Make it a habit to say it is important to, followed by a verb in the base form.
normal.cn: 记住句型 it is important to 后面接动词原形。

normal.en: More important and most important take extra words rather than -er and -est.
normal.cn: 比较级和最高级用 more、most，而不是加 -er、-est。

normal.en: An important role is a part in a task that the task cannot do without.
normal.cn: an important role 就是任务里少了它就做不成的那一份。

normal.en: Someone who is important in a field is not just busy but has weight in decisions.
normal.cn: 在某个领域里重要的人，不只是忙，而是在决定中有分量。

abstract.en: Importance is assigned by plans: what a plan depends on becomes important.
abstract.cn: 重要性由计划分配：计划所依赖的东西就变得重要。

abstract.en: The same word covers the serious and the pompous, so tone does much of the work.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既说郑重，也说装样子，因此大半靠语气来区分。

abstract.en: Calling something important is a small act of power, since it decides what people look at.
abstract.cn: 说某件事重要，本身就是一种小小的权力，因为它决定了大家看什么。

examples.en: It is important to check the figures twice before publishing the report.
examples.cn: 公布报告前，把数据核对两遍很重要。

examples.en: Her grandmother played an important role in her education.
examples.cn: 她的祖母在她的教育中起了重要作用。

examples.en: He tried hard to look important while holding the small envelope.
examples.cn: 他拿着那个小信封，努力装出一副总揽大局的样子。

dict_mnemonic.text: import 搬进来 + -ant 形容词词尾——值得搬上台面的，就是重要的

root: 拉丁语 importare「搬进来」（in + portare「搬运」）经中世纪拉丁语「关系重大」的引申、法语 important 进入英语，十六世纪起用于正式书面语，后进入日常口语并扩展到形容人物地位。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: mattering a great deal, having power in a field, and a manner that treats small things as great.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：事情分量重，某人在领域内有分量，以及把小事故意做大的神态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a slip of paper pushed to the centre of the table because everything today hangs on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张纸条被推到桌子正中央，因为今天的一切都系于它。

branches.en: THE WEIGHT: important describes things that must not be ignored.
branches.cn: 分量线：important 形容不可忽略的事物。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the adjective moves from matters to people with power.
branches.cn: 人物线：这个形容词从事转到有权势的人身上。

branches.en: THE ACT: an important nod is weight performed rather than carried.
branches.cn: 表演线：important 的一点头，是演出来的分量而非真分量。

branches.en: THE PATTERN: it is important to plus a verb is the most fixed frame.
branches.cn: 句型线：it is important to 加动词原形是最固定的框架。

branches.en: THE FAMILY: importance and importantly carry the same root into other word classes.
branches.cn: 词族线：importance 与 importantly 把同一词根带进别的词类。

intro.en: The table puts the -ant adjective ending next to the -ance and -ly forms of the family.
intro.cn: 此表把 -ant 形容词词尾放在同族的 -ance、-ly 形式旁边对照。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is importare, built from in and portare.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语底子是 importare，由 in 与 portare 组成。

items.example: This letter is important, so keep it safe.
They spoke about the importance of honesty.
items.exampleCN: 他们谈到了诚实的重要。
重要的是，全队达成了一致。

items.example: That is an unimportant detail for now.
items.exampleCN: 眼下那是个不重要的细节。

items.meaning: to send goods out of a country
items.example: The firm exports machines to Africa.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司向非洲出口机器。

items.example: The beam supports the whole roof.
items.exampleCN: 这根梁支撑着整个屋顶。

items.example: A portable lamp lit the tent.
items.exampleCN: 一盏便携灯照亮了帐篷。

latinEntries.meaning: a harbour, a place where goods are carried in
latinEntries.meaningCN: 拉丁语名词：港口，货物搬进之处

definition_zh: 户外的；室外的；露天的；户外用的
definition_en: happening, used or placed in the open air rather than inside a building
core_image: 学校后山草地上搭起的简易舞台，两旁的树当了幕布，观众就坐在草地上
scene: 春天一到，学校后山那片草地就成了舞台，孩子们把桌椅搬出去，在树荫下排节目。The school holds an outdoor concert on the grass every spring.
sceneCN: 这里 outdoor 是「户外的」（第 1 个义项：在建筑物之外举行）；句意为学校每年春天在草地上办一场户外音乐会，画面是后山草地上的简易舞台与坐着的观众。

pos.zh: 户外的；室外的；露天的；户外用的

derivatives.zh: 由 outdoor 去掉形容词用法、加副词词尾 -s 构成，义为「在露天；在户外」
由 outdoors 加形容词词尾 -y 构成，义为「喜欢户外活动的」
把 outdoor 的 out 换成 in 构成的同构反义词，义为「室内的」

senses.title: Happening in the open air
senses.definition: taking place outside a building rather than under a roof
senses.definitionCN: 在建筑物之外、而不是在屋顶之下举行
senses.example: The wedding was an outdoor ceremony in the garden.
senses.exampleCN: 那场婚礼是在花园里举行的户外仪式。
senses.why: The compound is out plus door, so whatever is outdoor happens beyond the doorway; the threshold is the line the word keeps pointing at.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词是 out 加 door，所以户外的事情都发生在门之外；门槛就是这个词一直指着的那条线，义项直接落在「门外」的空间上。

senses.title: Open to the sky, without a roof
senses.definition: describing a place or structure that has no roof and is open to the weather
senses.definitionCN: 形容场所或构筑物没有屋顶，直接对着天气敞开
senses.example: They ate at a long outdoor table beside the river.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在河边一张露天长桌旁吃饭。
senses.why: A place beyond the door with nothing over it is exposed to sun and rain, so the word can describe the shelter as well as the event.
senses.whyCN: 一个在门之外、头顶又空无一物的场所，就直接暴露在日晒雨淋之下，所以这个词既能说活动，也能说场所本身；露天义强调「没有遮蔽」这一层。

senses.title: Made for use outside
senses.definition: designed to be used in the open air, as clothes, furniture or equipment
senses.definitionCN: 专为在露天使用而设计，如衣物、家具或器材
senses.example: She bought a pair of outdoor shoes for the mountain trip.
senses.exampleCN: 她为这次登山买了一双户外鞋。
senses.why: Once the word marks the open air, makers label whatever is built to endure that weather, and the adjective shifts from place to purpose.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词标出了露天场所，制造商就把为那种天气而造的东西也标上它，形容词便从「地点」转向「用途」；户外装备义由此而来。

intro.en: Outdoor is a compound of two Old English words, out and door, shortened from the older phrase out of doors in the eighteenth century.
intro.cn: outdoor 是两个古英语词 out 与 door 的复合，十八世纪从较早的短语 out of doors 缩略而来。

items.en: The reconstructed forms ut and dur- gave both halves their Germanic shape, so the compound was built entirely inside English's own word family.
items.cn: 重构形式 ut 与 dur- 给了两半各自的日耳曼形态，整个复合词都建在英语自身的词族之内。

items.en: Out came from the adverb ut, and door from duru, the word for an opening that can be shut.
items.cn: out 出自副词 ut，door 出自名词 duru，后者指可以关上的一个开口。

items.en: Middle English already said out of doors for being in the open air, a phrase that kept door as the boundary of the house.
items.cn: 中古英语已经用 out of doors 表示「在露天」，这个短语仍把门当作屋子的边界。

items.en: The three-word phrase was shortened into the single attributive adjective outdoor, which then stood before nouns like life and games.
items.cn: 这个三词短语缩成了一个作定语的形容词 outdoor，随后站到 life、games 这类名词前面。

items.en: Modern English keeps outdoor for the adjective, outdoors for the adverb, and pairs the word with indoor on the other side of the wall.
items.cn: 现代英语把 outdoor 留给形容词、outdoors 留给副词，并让这个词与墙另一侧的 indoor 成对使用。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the compound's own family and its mirror opposite; the near-meaning group gathers words for air, outside space and open dining.
note.cn: 形近组收这个复合词自己的词族与镜像反义词；近义组收表示露天、外部空间与户外用餐的词。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning in the open air.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「在露天」的副词。

entries.definition: Existing or used inside a building.
entries.definitionCN: 在建筑物内存在或使用的。

entries.definition: Fond of activities in the open air.
entries.definitionCN: 喜欢户外活动的。

entries.definition: The older phrase from which outdoor was shortened.
entries.definitionCN: outdoor 由之缩略而成的较早短语。

entries.definition: Happening or existing outside, with no roof above.
entries.definitionCN: 在室外发生或存在、上方没有屋顶的。

entries.definition: Not inside a building, or the external part of something.
entries.definitionCN: 不在建筑物之内，或某物的外部。

entries.definition: In the open air, especially of eating.
entries.definitionCN: 在露天，尤指用餐。

entries.definition: The outer surface or side of something.
entries.definitionCN: 某物的外表面或外侧。

normalIntro.en: The word is a doorway turned into an adjective, so its hooks return to the door, the open sky beyond it, and the things made to survive out there.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是把一道门口变成形容词，记忆钩子都回到那扇门、门外的天空，以及为在门外存活而做的东西。

normal.en: Outdoor is simply out plus door, so the word points at everything on the other side of a doorway.
normal.cn: outdoor 就是 out 加 door，所以这个词指着门口另一侧的一切。

normal.en: The older phrase out of doors did the same work in three words before English shortened it into one adjective.
normal.cn: 较早的 out of doors 用三个词做同样的事，后来英语把它压成一个形容词。

normal.en: Outdoors is the adverb and outdoor the adjective, and that final s is the only difference between them.
normal.cn: outdoors 是副词，outdoor 是形容词，两者的差别只在末尾那个 s。

normal.en: Indoor is the mirror image built the same way with in, so the pair marks the two sides of one wall.
normal.cn: indoor 是用 in 按同样办法造出的镜像，这一对词标出同一道墙的两侧。

normal.en: Outdoor furniture and outdoor clothes are named for the weather they must endure, not for the place alone.
normal.cn: outdoor furniture 与 outdoor clothes 是按它们必须承受的天气命名，而不只是按地点命名。

abstract.en: A stage set on grass with trees standing in for curtains is the word at its clearest.
abstract.cn: 草地上搭起的舞台、拿树当幕布，就是这个词最清楚的样子。

abstract.en: A doorway with sun on one side and shadow on the other is the line the word draws.
abstract.cn: 一道门，一侧有阳光、一侧有阴影，就是这个词划出的界线。

abstract.en: A pair of boots left by a tent shows the adjective following a person out of the house.
abstract.cn: 帐篷旁放着的一双靴子，显示这个形容词跟着人走出了屋子。

examples.en: The school holds an outdoor concert on the grass every spring.
examples.cn: 学校每年春天在草地上办一场户外音乐会。

examples.en: They ate at a long outdoor table beside the river.
examples.cn: 他们在河边一张露天长桌旁吃饭。

examples.en: She bought a pair of outdoor shoes for the mountain trip.
examples.cn: 她为这次登山买了一双户外鞋。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥特多」——奥在门外，多是门；门外的这片天，就是户外。

root: outdoor 由古英语 ut（在外）与 duru（门）合成，十八世纪从短语 out of doors 缩略为形容词；两半都属日耳曼语词族，没有拉丁同源词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the far side of a door; the senses move from an event held there, to a place with no roof, to the gear made to be used out there.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是门的另一侧；义项从在那一侧举行的活动，转到没有屋顶的场所，再转到为在那一侧使用而造的装备。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rough stage on a grassy slope behind the school, trees standing in for curtains, the audience seated on the grass.
core.cn: 核心意象：学校后山坡草地上的简易舞台，树充当幕布，观众坐在草地上。

branches.en: a wedding standing on a garden lawn
branches.cn: 站在花园草坪上的婚礼

branches.en: a long table beside a river with no roof above
branches.cn: 河边上方无顶的长桌

branches.en: boots by a tent, made for wet ground
branches.cn: 帐篷旁为湿地而做的靴子

branches.en: one open space, used once for a ceremony and once for a meal
branches.cn: 同一片露天空地，一次用于仪式，一次用于吃饭

branches.en: clothing chosen for weather rather than for walls
branches.cn: 按天气而非按墙壁挑选的衣物

intro.en: The word joins an Old English adverb for outside with the Old English noun for door, then grows an adverb, an adjective and a mirror opposite from the same pattern.
intro.cn: 这个词把古英语中表示「在外」的副词与表示「门」的名词连在一起，再按同一模式长出副词、形容词与镜像反义词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 在户外；在露天；户外；露天场所；野外；大自然
definition_en: in or into the open air, outside a building; also the open air itself, especially when thought of as a place to live, work or play
core_image: 帐篷门帘被拉开，人一步跨出去，头顶突然空出一大片
scene: 清晨的营地，帐篷门帘被拉开，有人端着一杯热水走到草地上，抬头看没有屋顶的天空。She prefers to sleep outdoors whenever the weather allows.
sceneCN: 这里是「在户外、在露天」（第 1 个义项：在建筑物外面）；句意为只要天气允许，她更愿意睡在露天。图中可辨识物件：帐篷门帘、草地、热水杯。

pos.zh: 户外；露天场所；野外；大自然

derivatives.zh: 由 out 与 door 复合、再加 -s 构成副词；outdoor 是它的形容词形式，义为「户外的；露天的」
由 outdoors 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「喜爱户外活动的；适合户外的」
由旧短语 out of doors 连写而成，义为「在户外」，是 outdoors 的另一种写法

senses.title: Outside a building, in the open air
senses.definition: in or into the open air, on the far side of a door or wall rather than inside a building
senses.definitionCN: 在或进入建筑物之外的露天环境，也就是在门或墙的另一侧，而不是在屋里
senses.example: The children played outdoors until the light faded.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在户外玩到天光暗下来。
senses.why: The word is a compressed phrase: out of doors once meant literally passing through the door to the space beyond it, so the adverb still carries a step from inside to outside.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是短语压缩来的：out of doors 原意是「走出门去、到门外的空间」，所以这个副词到今天还带着从室内跨到室外的那一步。

senses.title: The open air as a place to be
senses.definition: the open air, thought of as a place where people spend time, work or rest, as in the outdoors
senses.definitionCN: 把露天的空气当作一个可以待着、干活或休息的地方，如 the outdoors
senses.example: After a week at a desk, he needed the outdoors.
senses.exampleCN: 在桌前坐了一周之后，他需要到户外去。
senses.why: Once the adverb had named the space beyond the door, English could put the definite article in front of it and treat that space as a place with a name, which is how the noun appeared.
senses.whyCN: 副词先给门外那片空间起了名，英语再在它前面加上定冠词，把那片空间当成一个有名字的地方，名词用法就是这样长出来的。

senses.title: Wild open country
senses.definition: open country with woods, hills or water, far from buildings, especially as a place for recreation
senses.definitionCN: 远离建筑的田野、树林、山岭或水域，尤指供人游玩休憩的开阔地带
senses.example: They spent the holiday exploring the great outdoors.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把这个假期用来探索广阔的大自然。
senses.why: The phrase the great outdoors added great to the same noun and pushed the meaning from any open air toward wide, unbuilt land, where the absence of roofs becomes the whole attraction.
senses.whyCN: the great outdoors 在同一个名词前加了 great，把意思从「任何露天的空气」推向开阔、没有建筑的土地；在那里，屋顶的缺席本身成了全部吸引力。

intro.en: Outdoors began as the phrase out of doors, a plain description of going through a door into the open, and the modern spelling fuses those words into one adverb and noun.
intro.cn: outdoors 起初是短语 out of doors，平平常常地描述「出了门到露天去」，现代拼写把这几个词粘成了一个副词和一个名词。

items.en: Old English had duru for a door and ūt for out, the two plain words that the later phrase would join.
items.cn: 古英语用 duru 表示门、用 ūt 表示向外，这两个平常的词后来被拼进同一个短语。

items.en: Middle English said out of dores, literally out of the doors, for leaving a house for the open air.
items.cn: 中古英语说 out of dores，字面就是「出了那些门」，用来表示离开屋子到露天去。

items.en: Writers began to set the phrase down as one word, outdoors, and to use it as an adverb of place.
items.cn: 到了十六、十七世纪，作者们把这个短语写成一个词 outdoors，用作表示地点的副词。

items.en: The fused form took a definite article and became a noun, the outdoors, naming the open air as a place rather than a direction.
items.cn: 这个合成形式带上定冠词，成了名词 the outdoors，把露天的空气当作一个地方来指，而不是一个方向。

items.en: Modern English adds the fixed phrase the great outdoors and uses the word for camping, sport and open-air work.
items.cn: 现代英语又添出固定说法 the great outdoors，并用这个词谈露营、运动和露天工作。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the door word and the forms built on the same compound; the near-meaning group collects other names for the air and land outside buildings.
note.cn: 形近组收表示门的词以及由同一复合结构长出的形式；近义组收其他表示「建筑物之外的空气与土地」的说法。

abstract.en: A roof is what the word leaves behind, and that absence is the whole point.

definition_en: extremely good and clearly above the usual standard, still owed or not yet paid, not yet done or settled, or easily noticed because it stands out
core_image: 一排人站在同一条白线后面，只有一个人往前多迈了半步，肩膀露在外面
scene: 答辩结束后的教室里，评审把一份厚厚的报告翻到最后一页，抬头看了看站在讲台边的年轻人。The committee gave her an award for outstanding research.
sceneCN: 这里的 outstanding 是「杰出的、出色的」（第 1 个义项：远高于一般水平）；句意为委员会因她出色的研究而给她颁奖。图中可辨识物件：厚报告、讲台、评审的笔。

pos.zh: 杰出的；未付的；未完成的；显著的

senses.title: Much better than others
senses.definition: extremely good and clearly above the usual standard, so that people notice and praise it
senses.definitionCN: 极好而明显高于一般水平，因而被人注意并称赞
senses.example: The committee gave her an award for outstanding research.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会因她出色的研究而给她颁奖。
senses.why: Outstanding is out plus standing: something that stands out from a row of others is seen first, and being seen first slowly turns into being admired.
senses.whyCN: outstanding 是 out 加 standing：在一排事物中「立在外面」的那一个最先被看见，而最先被看见就慢慢变成了被称赞。

senses.title: Still owed and not yet paid
senses.definition: of money or a bill, still owed to someone and not yet paid
senses.definitionCN: 指钱款或账单仍欠着别人、尚未付清
senses.example: The company has several outstanding debts.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司有几笔未偿债务。
senses.why: An unpaid debt is one that keeps standing there, unsettled, long after it should have been cleared, so the picture of standing out turns into standing open.
senses.whyCN: 一笔未付的债就是一直「立在那里」没有结清的账，本该了结却仍留在原处，于是「突出」的画面变成了「悬着未结」。

senses.title: Not yet done or settled
senses.definition: of work, problems or questions, not yet finished, answered or decided
senses.definitionCN: 指工作、问题或疑问尚未完成、回答或决定
senses.example: Two outstanding issues remain before the contract can be signed.
senses.exampleCN: 合同签署之前还有两个待解决的问题。
senses.why: Work that is finished leaves the desk; work still standing on it is the work not yet done, which is why the word covers pending tasks as well as unpaid money.
senses.whyCN: 做完的活会离开桌面，仍立在桌上的就是还没做完的活，所以这个词既能指待办的活儿，也能指没付的钱。

senses.title: Easily noticed, standing out clearly
senses.definition: clearly noticeable, especially as a feature of a thing, without any judgement of quality
senses.definitionCN: 明显引人注意，尤指某一事物的特征，并不含好坏评价
senses.example: The most outstanding feature of the design is its low roof.
senses.exampleCN: 这个设计最突出的特点是它低矮的屋顶。
senses.why: Here the word keeps its literal picture: the part that stands out from the rest is the part the eye catches first, whether it is good, bad or merely different.
senses.whyCN: 这里保留的是字面画面：从其余部分里凸出来的那块，就是眼睛最先抓住的那块，不管它好、坏还是仅仅不同。

intro.en: Outstanding is out plus standing, first recorded in the sixteenth century for something that projects or stands clear; the senses of unpaid money and of excellence grew out of that physical picture.
intro.cn: outstanding 是 out 加 standing，十六世纪最早记录时指「凸出、立在外面」的东西；未付的款项与卓越这两个义项都从这个身体可感的画面长出来。

items.en: Standan meant to stand or to take up a position, and it is the source of the modern verb stand.
items.cn: standan 意为站立、占据一个位置，是现代动词 stand 的来源。

items.en: Standing named the act of standing and also a person's position or rank.
items.cn: standing 既指站立这个动作，也指一个人的位置或名次。

items.en: The compound outstanding was used for something that projects beyond a surface or stands clear of others.
items.cn: 复合词 outstanding 用来指超出某个表面、或在其他东西之外立着的事物。

items.en: The word widened in two directions: a debt still standing unpaid, and a person or work that stands above the rest.
items.cn: 这个词向两个方向扩展：一是仍「立着」未付的账，二是高出其余的人或作品。

items.en: Modern English uses it for excellence, for money not yet paid, for matters not yet settled, and for any feature that stands out.
items.cn: 现代英语用它表示卓越、尚未支付的钱、尚未了结的事，以及任何突出的特征。

normalIntro.en: Outstanding rests on the plain physical fact of standing clear of a row, so its hooks keep that picture while the meanings travel towards money and praise.
normalIntro.cn: outstanding 建立在「从一排中站出来」这个朴素的实体画面之上，记忆钩子保留这个画面，让词义向金钱与赞美两头走。

normal.en: Outstanding is out plus standing, so the spelling already carries the picture of one thing standing clear of the rest.
normal.cn: outstanding 是 out 加 standing，拼写本身已经带着「某物立在其余之外」的画面。

normal.en: The money sense keeps the same picture: a debt stands there until it is settled, so it stays outstanding.
normal.cn: 金钱义保留同一画面：一笔债在结清之前一直立在原处，所以它是未付的。

normal.en: Outstandingly adds -ly and describes how well something was done, never how much money is owed.
normal.cn: outstandingly 加了 -ly，形容一件事做得多好，从不指欠了多少钱。

normal.en: Standout turns the two parts round for a person or thing that is obviously the best in a group.
normal.cn: standout 把两部分调过来，指一群中明显最好的那个人或那件东西。

normal.en: The old verb outstand is no longer used in ordinary English, so the adjective does the work alone.
normal.cn: 古动词 outstand 在现代英语里已不再使用，这项工作只由形容词独自承担。

abstract.en: A word built from standing suggests that excellence is often a matter of visibility: whatever stands out is noticed first.
abstract.cn: 一个从「站立」造出的词说明：卓越常常是可见度的问题，凡是站出来的，总被最先看到。

abstract.en: The same adjective covers praise and debt, which reminds us that what stands out can be either an honour or an obligation.
abstract.cn: 同一个形容词兼指赞美与欠款，这提醒人：站出来的东西，既可能是荣誉，也可能是义务。

abstract.en: One word holds both the best work and the unpaid bill, because both are things that refuse to leave the desk.
abstract.cn: 一个词同时装下最好的成果与未付的账单，因为这两样都不肯离开桌面。

examples.en: The committee gave her an award for outstanding research.
examples.cn: 委员会因她出色的研究而给她颁奖。

examples.en: The company has several outstanding debts.
examples.cn: 这家公司有几笔未偿债务。

examples.en: The most outstanding feature of the design is its low roof.
examples.cn: 这个设计最突出的特点是它低矮的屋顶。

root: 由 out（向外）与 standing（站立）复合，一般认为十六世纪出现，字面为「立在外面、凸出来」，由此分指显眼与卓越，以及仍「立着」未结清的账与未办完的事；stand 属日耳曼语词，无可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is one thing standing clear of a row; the senses divide into being admired for it, money still standing unpaid, work still standing unfinished, and a feature that simply stands out.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一样东西从一排之中站出来；义项按「因此被称赞」「钱仍立着未付」「活儿仍立着没完」「特征本身突出」分出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of people behind one white line, one of them half a step forward, a shoulder clear of the rest.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排人站在同一条白线后面，只有一个人往前多迈了半步，肩膀露在外面。

definition_en: an enclosed chamber that is heated so that food can be baked inside it, and by extension any similar heated chamber used in industry or felt as unbearable heat
core_image: 玻璃门内一团橙光，铁架上的面团正慢慢鼓起
scene: 冬夜的厨房里，玻璃门内透出橙黄的光，铁架上的面团一点点鼓起来。He lifted the lid and a wave of heat rolled out of the oven.
sceneCN: 这里 oven 是「烤箱」（第 1 个义项：家里用来烘焙食物的封闭炉箱）；句意为他掀开盖子，一股热气从烤箱里滚出来，画面是玻璃门内那团橙光和鼓起来的面团。

senses.title: A heated box for baking food at home
senses.definition: an enclosed part of a cooker, heated by gas or electricity, in which food is baked or roasted
senses.definitionCN: 炉灶上用燃气或电加热的封闭部分，用来烘烤或烤制食物
senses.example: She slid the tray into the hot oven and set the timer.
senses.exampleCN: 她把烤盘推进滚烫的烤箱，定了时。
senses.why: Old English ofen named a heated clay chamber, so the core picture is a closed box holding heat rather than a machine; baking is simply what such a box was built to do.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 ofen 指用火加热的泥土密室，所以这个词的底图是一只拢住热气的封闭箱子，而不是一台机器；烘焙只是这种箱子本来就承担的事，因此「烤箱」是最贴近底图的义项。

senses.title: The baking compartment of a cooker
senses.definition: the part of a kitchen stove that is closed off and heated for baking, as distinct from the burners on top
senses.definitionCN: 厨房炉灶上封闭加热、专门用于烘烤的部分，与上方的明火灶眼相对
senses.example: The casserole sat in the lower oven of the cooker.
senses.exampleCN: 炖锅放在炉灶下面那层烤室里。
senses.why: A cooker repeats the old chamber in miniature and puts it under the burners, so the word moves from a whole hearth to one compartment of a kitchen range.
senses.whyCN: 炉灶把旧式的加热室缩小后安在灶眼下面，于是这个词从整座火塘转到厨房灶具的一个隔间；词义缩小，指的还是那只装热气的箱子。

senses.title: An industrial chamber for firing or drying
senses.definition: a large heated chamber used in industry for firing clay, drying materials or turning coal into coke
senses.definitionCN: 工业上用的大型加热室，用于烧制陶土、烘干物料或把煤炼成焦炭
senses.example: A coke oven burns coal slowly to produce coke for steel making.
senses.exampleCN: 炼焦炉把煤慢慢加热，为炼钢生产焦炭。
senses.why: Brick ovens and coke ovens enlarge the same chamber and trap heat around clay or coal instead of dough, so the name follows the shape of the box rather than the food inside.
senses.whyCN: 砖窑与炼焦炉把同一只加热室放大，把热气拢在陶土或煤的周围而不是面团周围；名字跟着箱子的形状走，不跟着里面的东西走，于是义项从厨房扩到工厂。

senses.title: A room or place that feels unbearably hot
senses.definition: a room or enclosed space that is so hot and airless that it feels like the inside of an oven
senses.definitionCN: 热而不透风的房间或封闭空间，待在里面像待在烤箱里一样
senses.example: The attic was an oven by noon.
senses.exampleCN: 到了中午，阁楼热得像烤箱。
senses.why: The comparison works by sensation rather than by cooking: a person standing in a closed hot room feels the same blast that comes out when an oven door opens, so the word crosses over to discomfort.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻靠的是体感而不是烹饪：人站在不透风的闷热房间里，感到的正是烤箱门打开时扑出的那股热浪，所以这个词跨到「难受的闷热」这一边。

intro.en: Oven is an inherited Germanic word for a heated chamber, and its recorded history in English reaches back to the first written texts.
intro.cn: oven 是日耳曼语中表示「加热密室」的固有词，它在英语里的记录可以上溯到最早的文献。

items.en: A form usually reconstructed as ufnaz or uhnaz gave the Germanic languages their word for a baking chamber, though the exact shape of the reconstruction is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般把日耳曼语的这个词重构为 ufnaz 或 uhnaz，意为烘焙用的加热室，但重构的确切形式仍有争议。

items.en: Old English ofen named a dome-shaped chamber of clay or stone with a fire lit inside it.
items.cn: 古英语 ofen 指圆顶的泥土或石头加热室，火就生在室内。

items.en: Middle English kept both the sense and the spelling, and a village often shared one large oven for the whole week's bread.
items.cn: 中古英语保留原义与原拼写，一个村子常常共用一座大炉烤一整周的面包。

items.en: Iron ranges brought a smaller oven indoors beside the fire, and the word settled into the kitchen.
items.cn: 铁炉灶把较小的烤室搬进室内、安在火边，这个词就此落进厨房。

items.en: Gas, electric and microwave ovens still name the same closed chamber, while a sweltering room is also called an oven.
items.cn: 燃气炉、电烤箱与微波炉沿用的仍是那只封闭加热室，而闷热的房间也被叫作 oven。

note.en: The look-alike group collects compounds built directly on the noun; the near-meaning group collects other chambers and appliances that produce or hold heat.
note.cn: 形近组收直接由这个名词构成的复合词；近义组收其他产生热量或拢住热量的炉具与炉室。

entries.definitionCN: 用于供暖或熔炼材料的高温封闭炉。

entries.definitionCN: 用于高温烧制陶器、砖或石灰的窑。

entries.definition: An appliance that heats food with electromagnetic waves instead of a flame.
entries.definitionCN: 用电磁波而非明火加热食物的炉具。

normalIntro.en: The word names a box that holds heat, and its hooks return to the chamber, its fuel and the compounds built on it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词说的是「拢住热气的箱子」，记忆钩子都回到那间加热室、它的燃料，以及由它构成的复合词。

normal.en: Old English ofen and German Ofen are cousins, so the word has meant a heated chamber for more than a thousand years.
normal.cn: 古英语 ofen 与德语 Ofen 是同源词，所以这个词指加热室已有一千多年。

normal.en: The noun names the box, not the fuel, which is why wood, gas and electric versions all keep one name.
normal.cn: 这个名词命名的是箱子而不是燃料，所以柴火、燃气与电热的版本共用一个名字。

normal.en: Ovenproof adds a suffix meaning resistant, so the word describes what the heat cannot do to the dish.
normal.cn: ovenproof 加上表示「抗得住」的后缀，说的是高温拿这只盘子没办法。

normal.en: Microwave oven puts the new heating method in front of the old noun instead of inventing a fresh word.
normal.cn: microwave oven 把新的加热方式摆在旧名词前面，而没有另造新词。

normal.en: A room called an oven borrows only the heat of the box, not its shape or its purpose.
normal.cn: 被叫作 oven 的房间只借了箱子的热度，不借它的形状与用途。

abstract.en: A glass door glowing orange in a dark kitchen is the word at its plainest.
abstract.cn: 暗厨房里一扇透出橙光的玻璃门，就是这个词最朴素的样子。

abstract.en: A baker drawing a long wooden peel out of a brick mouth shows the word before it entered the kitchen.
abstract.cn: 面包师从砖砌炉口抽出长木铲，显示这个词走进厨房之前的样子。

abstract.en: A closed attic at noon shows the word sliding from cooking to plain discomfort.
abstract.cn: 正午紧闭的阁楼，显示这个词从烹饪滑向单纯的难受。

definition_zh: 克服；战胜；压倒；使受不了
definition_en: to deal successfully with a difficulty, to defeat an opponent, or to make someone helpless with a strong feeling or with fumes and heat
core_image: 一个人顶着风爬到最后一道坡顶，身后是散开的队伍
scene: 山口的雪还没化，队伍里有人喘得说不出话，领队回头指了指前面那道坡。The team overcame the last steep section just before dark.
sceneCN: 这里 overcame 是「克服」（第 1 个义项：把困难顶过去）；句意为队伍在天黑前越过了最后一段陡坡，画面是山口残雪与喘着气的人。

pos.zh: 克服；战胜；压倒；使受不了

derivatives.zh: 由 overcome 加表示人的后缀 -er 构成，义为「克服者；战胜者」
由 overcome 加 -ing 构成的动名词，义为「克服；战胜的过程」

senses.title: To deal successfully with a difficulty
senses.definition: to succeed in dealing with a problem, obstacle or difficult condition that stands in the way
senses.definitionCN: 成功处理挡在面前的难题、障碍或艰难处境
senses.example: She had to overcome her fear of heights before she could cross the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 她得先克服恐高，才敢走过那座桥。
senses.why: The oldest form of the verb is over plus come, meaning to arrive on top of something; a difficulty is treated as ground a person has to get across, so success is pictured as reaching the other side.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词最早是 over 加 come，意为「来到某物之上」；困难被当成一片必须走过去的土地，所以「克服」在画面上就是走到了对面。

senses.title: To defeat an opponent
senses.definition: to get the better of an enemy or rival in a contest, fight or argument
senses.definitionCN: 在竞赛、打斗或争论中压过对手或敌手
senses.example: He overcame his opponent in three straight sets.
senses.exampleCN: 他连下三盘战胜了对手。
senses.why: If coming over something can mean standing on top of it, the same movement serves for a rival: the winner is the one left standing over the other, and the sporting sense follows.
senses.whyCN: 既然「来到某物之上」可以指站到它上面，同一个动作也能用在对手身上：赢家是最后站着、把对方压在下面的那个人，竞技义就由此而来。

senses.title: To make someone helpless with feeling or fumes
senses.definition: usually in the passive, to affect someone so strongly with emotion, heat or fumes that they lose control of themselves
senses.definitionCN: 常用于被动式，指被情绪、热气或烟味冲击到失去自持
senses.example: She was overcome with relief when the results arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 结果传来时，她松了一口气，几乎站不住。
senses.why: A person who is overcome has been come over by something heavier than a task; the same verb that marks getting on top of a problem marks a feeling getting on top of the person.
senses.whyCN: 被 overcome 的人，是被某种比任务更沉的东西压在上面；同一个动词既表示人爬到问题之上，也表示情绪爬到人之上，被动式于是有了「被压倒」的一面。

senses.title: To come upon suddenly, as in older usage
senses.definition: in older writing, to come upon someone or something suddenly, without the modern idea of winning
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的文字里指突然来到某人或某物身上，不含现代「取胜」的意思
senses.example: A great weariness overcame the travellers at dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 黄昏时，一阵极度的疲惫袭向这些旅人。
senses.why: This is the literal layer that the other senses grew from: over as arrival upon a place, with no struggle yet implied, preserved in a few literary phrases.
senses.whyCN: 这是其余义项生长出来的字面层：over 表示「来到某处之上」，此时还没有争胜的意味，只在少数书面说法里保留下来。

intro.en: Overcome was made inside English from two inherited words, and its history runs from plain arrival to victory and then to being flattened by feeling.
intro.cn: overcome 由两个英语固有词在英语内部合成，词义从「到达」走到「取胜」，再走到「被情绪压垮」。

items.en: Over and come both descend from reconstructed Germanic forms, so the compound belongs to the inherited vocabulary rather than to borrowed Latin.
items.cn: over 与 come 都上溯到重构的日耳曼语形式，所以这个复合词属于固有词汇，不是从拉丁语借来的。

items.en: Old English ofercuman meant to come upon a person or place, and from that contact it also meant to get the better of someone.
items.cn: 古英语 ofercuman 指来到某人或某地之上，又从这种接触引申出压过对方的意思。

items.en: Middle English pushed the verb toward victory in battle and success against an obstacle, while the plain arrival sense faded.
items.cn: 中古英语把这个动词推向战场上的胜利与对障碍的克服，单纯的「到达」义则淡出。

items.en: The passive pattern be overcome with gave the word a new task, describing a person flattened by grief, heat or fumes.
items.cn: 被动结构 be overcome with 给了这个词新任务，用来描述被悲伤、热气或烟味压垮的人。

items.en: Modern English keeps the active sense of mastering a problem and the passive sense of being overwhelmed, plus an archaic use for coming upon.
items.cn: 现代英语保留主动的「解决问题」与被动的「被压倒」，另有一层古旧的「突然降临」用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the same verb and other compounds built with over; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of winning and of being overwhelmed.
note.cn: 形近组收同一动词的各种形式，以及用 over 构成的其他复合词；近义组收表示取胜与被压垮的动词。

entries.definition: The past tense of the verb, used for a victory already won.
entries.definitionCN: 这个动词的过去式，用于已经取得的胜利。

entries.definition: The present participle, used for the process still going on.
entries.definitionCN: 现在分词，用于仍在进行的过程。

entries.definition: To do too much, or to cook something for too long.
entries.definitionCN: 做得过多，或把东西煮得过久。

entries.definition: To put too much weight or too many demands on something.
entries.definitionCN: 给某物加上过重的负担或过多的要求。

entries.definition: To take control of a place or people by force.
entries.definitionCN: 以武力控制某地或某人。

entries.definition: To beat someone in a battle, game or election.
entries.definitionCN: 在战斗、比赛或选举中击败某人。

entries.definition: To deal successfully with a difficulty or obstacle.
entries.definitionCN: 成功处理困难或障碍。

entries.definition: To affect someone so strongly that they cannot think or act.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈影响某人，使其无法思考或行动。

normalIntro.en: The word is over plus come, and its hooks return to that arrival, to the fight, and to the feeling that arrives on top of a person.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 over 加 come，记忆钩子都回到那次「到达」、那场争斗，以及压到人头上的情绪。

normal.en: Over and come are both native Germanic words, so overcome was assembled in English rather than borrowed whole.
normal.cn: over 与 come 都是日耳曼语固有词，所以 overcome 是在英语里拼起来的，不是整体借入的。

normal.en: The oldest sense is arrival, which is why an old sentence can say that weariness overcame someone without any fight.
normal.cn: 最老的一层意思是「到达」，所以旧句里可以说疲惫袭向某人，而不含争斗。

normal.en: Victory is pictured as standing over the other person, and that picture produced the modern sense of defeating.
normal.cn: 胜利被画成站在对方之上，这幅画产出了现代的「击败」义。

normal.en: The passive be overcome with keeps the same downward pressure: the feeling is now the thing on top.
normal.cn: 被动式 be overcome with 保留了同一股向下的压力，只是这回压在上面的是情绪。

normal.en: Overdo and overload share the prefix but not the victory, which shows how far over can stretch.
normal.cn: overdo 与 overload 共用前缀却没有胜负之意，可见 over 能拉得多远。

abstract.en: A climber topping the last ridge with the wind at his back is the word at its plainest.
abstract.cn: 登山者顶着风翻过最后一道山脊，就是这个词最朴素的样子。

abstract.en: A wrestler left standing over his rival turns arrival into victory.
abstract.cn: 摔跤手站在对手之上，把「到达」变成了「取胜」。

abstract.en: A letter read at the door, hand shaking, shows how a feeling can arrive on top of a person.
abstract.cn: 在门口读信、手发抖，说明一种情绪如何压到人身上。

examples.en: She had to overcome her fear of heights before she could cross the bridge.
examples.cn: 她得先克服恐高，才敢走过那座桥。

examples.en: He overcame his opponent in three straight sets.
examples.cn: 他连下三盘战胜了对手。

examples.en: She was overcome with relief when the results arrived.
examples.cn: 结果传来时，她松了一口气，几乎站不住。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧沃康」——欧沃扛着难事往前走，总算跨了过去。

root: overcome 由古英语 ofer（在上、越过）与 cuman（来）合成，原义为「来到……之上」，后引申为「压过、战胜」；两半都是日耳曼语固有词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is arriving on top of something; the senses run from crossing a difficulty, to standing over a rival, to a feeling standing over the person, and back to the old literal arrival.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「来到某物之上」；义项从越过困难，到站到对手之上，到情绪压到人头上，再回到古老的「突然降临」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a walker topping the last ridge against the wind, the rest of the group scattered behind.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人顶着风爬到最后一道山脊，队伍散在他身后。

branches.en: a walker forcing his way up the final slope
branches.cn: 登山者硬撑着爬上最后一段坡

branches.en: a wrestler left standing over his rival
branches.cn: 摔跤手站在对手之上

branches.en: a person reading a letter with a shaking hand
branches.cn: 手抖着读信的人

branches.en: weariness arriving at dusk with no struggle at all
branches.cn: 黄昏时毫无争斗地袭来的疲惫

branches.en: one pressure, once pushed against and once suffered
branches.cn: 同一种压力，一次被顶回去，一次被承受

intro.en: The word joins the Old English prefix for over with the verb to come, then feeds a small family of forms and other over- compounds.
intro.cn: 这个词把古英语中表示「在上」的前缀与动词「来」连在一起，再由它生出几个形式与别的 over 复合词。

latinIntro.en: The word is a Germanic compound with no Latin family of its own; Latin super is only a distant relative of the prefix over, not a member of this word's family.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是日耳曼语复合词，本身没有拉丁词族；拉丁语 super 只是前缀 over 的远亲，不算这个词族的成员。

items.meaningCN: 把动词变成名词的词尾

definition_zh: 海外的；国外的；在海外；向海外；（总称）海外地区
definition_en: located, happening, or living across the sea in a foreign country; also the foreign countries taken together as a region
core_image: 站在海岸线上，越过一条水带望向另一块陆地
scene: 港口堆场里，贴着外文标签的集装箱被吊上货轮。The shipping clerk wrote overseas on the destination line, and the crane lifted the last box toward the sea.
sceneCN: 这里 overseas 是「海外的、国外的」（第 1 个义项：位于国外）；句意：报关员在目的地一栏写下“海外”，吊机把最后一个箱子吊向大海。图中可辨识物件：集装箱、外文标签、吊机、货轮、报关单、海平线；对应第 1 个义项。

derivatives.zh: 海外的（较早的变体拼法）
总部或驻地在海外的
在海外受训的
驶往海外的；发往国外的
在海外出生的

senses.title: Across the sea: located abroad
senses.definition: located or based in a country across the sea from the speaker's own
senses.definitionCN: 位于说话者本国之外、隔海相望的国家
senses.example: The company has three overseas branches.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司有三家海外分公司。
senses.why: Over- means across or beyond, and sea is the water between the two shores. The reference point is always the speaker's own coast; what matters lies on the far side of the water.
senses.whyCN: over- 是“越过、在那边”，sea 是两岸之间的水。参照点始终是说话者自己这一侧的海岸，重要的事物在水的那一边。

senses.title: Coming from abroad
senses.definition: coming from or belonging to a foreign country
senses.definitionCN: 来自外国或属于外国的
senses.example: Overseas visitors filled the museum.
senses.exampleCN: 海外游客挤满了博物馆。
senses.why: Here the direction reverses: the word marks not where the thing sits but where it came from. The sea is still the divider, only now the traffic crosses toward the speaker.
senses.whyCN: 这里方向反了过来：词标记的不是事物所在之处，而是它来自何处。海仍是分界，只是人流物流朝说话者这一侧越过来。

senses.title: Abroad: the adverbial direction
senses.definition: to or in a country across the sea
senses.definitionCN: 到海外，或在海外
senses.example: She moved overseas after graduation.
senses.exampleCN: 毕业后她移居海外。
senses.why: English lets the same compound serve as an adverb without adding -ly. The phrase names a path, and the path crosses water, so no separate adverb form was ever needed.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许同一个复合词直接作副词，不必加 -ly。这个短语命名的是一条路径，而路径要越过水，因此从来不需要另造副词形式。

senses.title: The overseas as a named region
senses.definition: the countries beyond the sea, taken together as a region or sphere of activity
senses.definitionCN: 隔海之外的国家，作为一个地区或活动领域的总称
senses.example: Sales in the overseas grew faster than at home.
senses.exampleCN: 海外市场的销售增长快于国内。
senses.why: A locational phrase can be nominalized: the far side stops being a direction and becomes a territory with a name. Business and journalism then speak of the overseas as a single place with its own figures.
senses.whyCN: 方位短语可以名词化：那边不再是方向，而变成一块有名字的地盘。商业与新闻于是把“海外”当作一个有自己的数字的单一地方来谈。

senses.title: Foreign affairs: the official sphere
senses.definition: relating to a country's interests and activities beyond its borders
senses.definitionCN: 涉及一国国境之外的利益与活动
senses.example: The ministry handles overseas affairs.
senses.exampleCN: 该部负责海外事务。
senses.why: Bureaucracy names the foreign sphere as an adjective, and activities there become a department's remit. The word turns geography into an administrative portfolio.
senses.whyCN: 官僚体系用形容词命名对外领域，那边的活动就变成一个部门的职责。这个词把地理变成了一份行政分工。

senses.title: Living abroad: of people
senses.definition: of a person or community, living in a foreign country
senses.definitionCN: 指个人或群体侨居外国
senses.example: Overseas Chinese communities kept the festival alive.
senses.exampleCN: 海外华人社群把这个节日保留了下来。
senses.why: For people the compound marks residence rather than origin: the person's daily life has moved to the far shore, even if the passport and the language have not.
senses.whyCN: 用于人时，这个词标记的是“居住地”而不是“来源地”：此人的日常生活已经移到海那边，即使护照与语言没有跟着变。

senses.title: Military deployment beyond the sea
senses.definition: of troops or bases, stationed in a foreign country
senses.definitionCN: 指部队或基地驻扎在外国
senses.example: The unit served on overseas deployment for a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这支部队在海外部署了一年。
senses.why: Armies inherit the maritime image even when they fly. Overseas still means outside the home territory, and the word keeps military language politely vague about which country is meant.
senses.whyCN: 军队即使坐飞机也继承了这个航海意象。overseas 仍指本国领土之外，同时让军事语言礼貌地含糊，不必点明是哪一个国家。

senses.title: Historical euphemism: the colonies
senses.definition: in British usage, a polite word for the colonies and dominions, especially in the early twentieth century
senses.definitionCN: 英国用法中，对殖民地与自治领的委婉说法，尤见于 20 世纪早期
senses.example: Wartime posters promised work in the overseas dominions.
senses.exampleCN: 战时海报承诺在海外自治领有工作机会。
senses.why: Overseas let speakers avoid the word colony. Distance across water replaced a political relationship that many preferred not to name, which is how a neutral geographic term became an instrument of imperial tact.
senses.whyCN: overseas 让说话者避开“colony”这个词。隔海的距离替代了一段许多人不想点明的政治关系，于是一个中性的地理词变成了帝国辞令里的委婉工具。

intro.en: Overseas is a native English compound of over and sea. The word is transparent, but the deeper origin of sea itself is not certain.
intro.cn: overseas 是 over 与 sea 构成的英语本族复合词。词形透明，但 sea 本身的更早来源并不确定。

items.en: The older form oversea is recorded as an adjective and adverb meaning 'across the sea, on the other side of the sea'.
items.cn: 较早的形式 oversea 记录于 15 世纪，作形容词与副词，意为“隔海、在海的那一边”。

items.en: Overseas appears with the same meaning and eventually displaces oversea in most contexts. Both are simply over + sea.
items.cn: overseas 于 16 世纪 80 年代出现，意义相同，最终在多数语境中取代 oversea。两者都只是 over + sea。

items.en: British imperial usage makes overseas a euphemism for the colonies and dominions, especially during the First World War.
items.cn: 英国帝国用语把 overseas 变成殖民地与自治领的委婉说法，尤在第一次世界大战期间。

items.en: The noun use is recorded: the overseas as the collective name for territories beyond the sea.
items.cn: 名词用法记录于 1919 年：the overseas 作为隔海之外领土的集合名称。

items.en: Trade, education, and the military keep the word busy: overseas market, overseas students, overseas deployment. The geographic frame stays neutral, which is exactly why it survives.
items.cn: 贸易、教育与军事让这个词持续活跃：海外市场、留学生、海外部署。它的地理框架保持中性，这也正是它存活下来的原因。

note.en: The first group collects over- words that look similar but do not mean across the sea. The second compares words for foreignness and distance.
note.cn: 第一组是同样带 over-、外形相近却不表示“隔海”的词。第二组比较表示“异国、远方”的词。

entries.definition: to watch over and supervise work or people. It sounds almost the same but has no sea in it.
entries.definitionCN: 监督、管理工作的进行。读音几乎相同，但里面没有 sea。

entries.definition: larger than the standard size. It shares over- and the -size ending but means excess, not distance.
entries.definitionCN: 超过标准尺寸的。它同样带 over- 和 -size 结尾，但表示“过大”，而不是距离。

entries.definition: to express something more strongly than is justified. Its over- means too much, not across.
entries.definitionCN: 把话说得过头；夸大。它的 over- 表示“过分”，不是“越过”。

entries.definition: a loose garment worn over other clothes. It is over + all, and the plural -s can be mistaken for the -s of overseas.
entries.definitionCN: 穿在其他衣服外面的宽松工装。它是 over + all，复数 -s 容易被误当成 overseas 的 -s。

entries.definition: in or to a foreign country. It is only an adverb, while overseas can also be an adjective and a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 在外国、到外国。它只能作副词，而 overseas 还能作形容词和名词。

entries.definition: belonging to a country other than one's own. It is the plain adjective and needs no sea, while overseas keeps the maritime image.
entries.definitionCN: 属于本国以外国家的。它是最朴素的形容词，不需要海；overseas 则保留了航海意象。

entries.definition: involving two or more nations. It stresses relations between states, while overseas stresses distance from home.
entries.definitionCN: 涉及两个或多个国家的。它强调国家之间的关系，overseas 强调与本土的距离。

entries.definition: away from the shore, especially of islands used for financial reasons. It is about distance from land, not about another country.
entries.definitionCN: 离岸的，尤指用于金融目的的海岛。它说的是离开陆地，而不是到另一个国家。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on the over + sea picture, then three abstract images about distance and how it is used.
normalIntro.cn: 先用五个围绕 over + sea 画面的挂钩，再用三个关于距离及其用法的抽象画面。

normal.en: Say it as over-seas: over the seas, not over the sees. The plural seas are the water you cross.
normal.cn: 把它读成 over-seas：越过一片片海，而不是 over the sees。复数 seas 就是你越过的水。

normal.en: Look at a map: your finger starts on the home coast, crosses blue, and lands on another country. That finger path is overseas.
normal.cn: 看地图：手指从本国海岸出发，越过蓝色，落到另一个国家。那条手指路径就是 overseas。

normal.en: overseas students are students who crossed the sea to study; the sea is in the name, not in their luggage.
normal.cn: overseas students 是越过海来读书的学生；海在名字里，不在他们的行李里。

normal.en: The word has no -ly adverb form because it already works as an adverb: go overseas, live overseas.
normal.cn: 这个词没有 -ly 副词形式，因为它本身就能作副词：go overseas、live overseas。

normal.en: Overseas trade is trade that leaves the harbour; if the goods never touch water, the word still keeps the old picture.
normal.cn: overseas trade 是离开港口的贸易；即使货物从不碰水，这个词仍保留着旧画面。

abstract.en: Overseas is distance turned into a category: the far shore becomes an administrative box.
abstract.cn: overseas 是把距离变成一个分类：远岸被装进一个行政抽屉。

abstract.en: Every overseas is someone's home. The word marks the speaker's shore, not an absolute edge of the world.
abstract.cn: 每一个“海外”都是某些人的家。这个词标记的是说话者的海岸，而不是世界的绝对边缘。

abstract.en: The word is neutral geography doing political work: it can name a colony without saying colony.
abstract.cn: 这个词让中性的地理替政治干活：它可以指殖民地，却不必说出 colony。

examples.en: The firm opened an overseas office in Osaka last spring.
examples.cn: 这家公司去年春天在大阪开设了海外办事处。

examples.en: Many overseas students work part-time while they improve their English.
examples.cn: 许多留学生在提高英语的同时做兼职。

examples.en: The letters went overseas by ship and took six weeks to arrive.
examples.cn: 这些信件经海路寄往海外，走了六周才到。

dict_mnemonic.note: 把 over 记成“越过”，sea 记成“海”：越过海的那一边，就是海外。
dict_mnemonic.text: over（越过）+ sea（海）+ -s → 海外的、在海外；海外地区

root: over（越过）+ sea（海）；sea 是日耳曼语固有词，更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The senses follow the direction of travel: first something sits on the far shore, then it comes toward the speaker, then the word becomes a path, a named region, an official portfolio, a way of living, a military station, and finally a polite imperial word for the colonies.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项顺着旅行的方向展开：先有东西位于远岸，再有东西朝说话者这边来，随后这个词变成一条路径、一块被命名的地区、一份官方职责、一种居住方式、一处军事驻地，最后成为帝国辞令里对殖民地的委婉说法。

core.en: A coastline, a band of water, and another land on the far side
core.cn: 一条海岸线、一条水带，以及水那边另一块陆地

branches.en: A place across the sea: the word locates something abroad.
branches.cn: 海那边的地方：这个词指某物位于国外。

branches.en: From a path to a place: the adverb of movement becomes a named region.
branches.cn: 从路径到地方：表示移动的副词变成一块被命名的地区。

branches.en: The official sphere: foreign affairs at a desk, and troops in the field.
branches.cn: 官方领域：办公桌上的对外事务，以及战场上的海外驻军。

branches.en: People: those who live and work across the sea.
branches.cn: 人：在海外生活与工作的那些人。

branches.en: Origin and old tongue: goods that come from across the sea, and the older British label for the colonies.
branches.cn: 来源与旧称：从海那边来的货物，以及英国旧时对殖民地的说法。

intro.en: Overseas is built from the over- prefix and the sea family. The items below include both true relatives and the nearest sea compounds, so the boundary of the family is visible.
intro.cn: overseas 由 over- 前缀和 sea 词族构成。下面既有真正的同族词，也有最接近的海事复合词，以便看清词族的边界。

latinIntro.en: No Latin entry applies: over is Old English ofer (PIE *uper), and sea is Old English sæ, from Proto-Germanic *saiwiz, whose deeper origin is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 不适用拉丁词条：over 是古英语 ofer（原始印欧语 *uper），sea 是古英语 sæ，来自原始日耳曼语 *saiwiz，其更早来源不确定。

items.meaning: across the sea; in or from a foreign country
items.meaningCN: 隔海；在海外或来自海外

items.meaning: the earlier adjective and adverb, now mostly replaced
items.meaningCN: 较早的形容词与副词形式，现已多被取代
items.example: An oversea cable was laid in 1866.
items.exampleCN: 一条海底电缆于 1866 年铺设。

items.meaning: the salt water that covers most of the earth
items.meaningCN: 覆盖地球大部分区域的咸水
items.example: The sea was calm that morning.
The seaward window caught the wind.

items.meaning: working or traveling on the sea
items.example: A seafaring family kept the old charts.
items.exampleCN: 一个航海世家保存着旧海图。

items.meaning: away from the shore; of financial islands
items.meaningCN: 离岸的；金融意义上的离岸

items.example: A transoceanic flight takes twelve hours.
items.exampleCN: 跨洋飞行需要十二小时。

definition_zh: 自己的；本人的；自己的东西；拥有；承认
definition_en: belonging to oneself, the thing that belongs to oneself, and to have something as property or to admit a fact
core_image: 钥匙串上那把只配你家门的钥匙
scene: 搬家那天，每只纸箱上都写着同一个名字。After the move she kept her own keys in a small tin box.
sceneCN: 这里 own 是「自己的」（第 1 个义项：属于本人的）；句意为搬完之后，她把自己的钥匙收在一只小铁盒里。图中可辨识物件：纸箱、钥匙、铁盒。

pos.zh: 自己的东西（用在物主词之后）

derivatives.zh: 由 own 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -er 构成，指拥有某物的人
由 owner 加 -ship 构成，指所有权、产权
home 与 owner 复合而成，指自有住房者

senses.title: Belonging to a particular person
senses.definition: belonging to a particular person rather than to anyone else
senses.definitionCN: 属于某个特定的人，而不是任何别人
senses.example: She keeps her own keys in a small tin box.
senses.exampleCN: 她把自己的钥匙放在一个小铁盒里。
senses.why: The adjective began as a past participle meaning possessed; it points back at the person who holds the thing, so it always answers the question whose.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词最初是表示「被拥有」的过去分词；它回指持有东西的那个人，所以总在回答「谁的」这一问题。

senses.title: The thing that belongs to oneself
senses.definition: used after a possessive word to mean the particular thing or person that belongs to someone
senses.definitionCN: 用在物主词之后，指属于某人的那样东西或那个人
senses.example: He wanted a desk of his own, away from the shared one.
senses.exampleCN: 他想要一张属于自己的桌子，不再和人共用。
senses.why: When the noun is already clear from context, own can stand alone after words like my or his, carrying the idea of possession without naming the object again.
senses.whyCN: 当名词已由上下文点明，own 可以跟在 my、his 这类物主词后单独使用，重复「属于」这层意思而不再说出物品的名字。

senses.title: To have something as property
senses.definition: to legally or actually have something as property
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上或事实上把某物作为财产持有
senses.example: Her family owns a small orchard outside the town.
senses.exampleCN: 她家在城外拥有一片小果园。
senses.why: The verb comes from the same Old English word for having and holding; possession is the plain centre that the adjective later uses to point at a person.
senses.whyCN: 动词来自同一个表示「持有、拥有」的古英语词；持有正是这个词最朴素的中心，形容词后来只是用它回指持有的人。

senses.title: To admit a fact or fault
senses.definition: to admit that something is true, especially something you would rather not say
senses.definitionCN: 承认某事为真，尤指本不愿说出口的事
senses.example: She owned that the plan had been too rushed.
senses.exampleCN: 她承认那个计划太仓促了。
senses.why: To own a fact is to accept it as part of what is yours, which is why British English uses own up for confessing a fault.
senses.whyCN: 承认一个事实，就是把它当成属于自己的东西接受下来；英式英语里 own up 表示坦白，正由此而来。

intro.en: Own has two faces: an Old English past participle meaning possessed, which became the adjective, and an Old English verb meaning to have, which became the modern verb.
intro.cn: own 有两副面孔：一个是表示「被拥有」的古英语过去分词，后来成了形容词；另一个是表示「持有」的古英语动词，后来成了今天的动词。

items.en: The adjective āgen was a past participle of the verb āgan and meant possessed or belonging to someone.
items.cn: 形容词 āgen 是动词 āgan 的过去分词，意为「被拥有的、属于某人的」。

items.en: The verb āgan meant to have, to hold and to own land or goods, and it is also the source of owe.
items.cn: 动词 āgan 意为持有、握着，拥有土地或财物，它同时也是 owe 的来源。

items.en: Middle English owen served as both adjective and verb, and the spelling with w replaced the old g sound in writing.
items.cn: 中古英语的 owen 同时作形容词和动词，书写上用 w 代替了旧的 g 音。

items.en: Own up appears in the sense of admitting a fault, extending possession to the idea of accepting a fact as one's own.
items.cn: own up 在十六世纪出现「承认过失」的意思，把「拥有」扩展到「把事实认作自己的」。

items.en: Modern English keeps own as adjective, pronoun and verb, while the related verb owe carries the debt side of the old word.
items.cn: 现代英语让 own 同时作形容词、代词和动词，而由同一旧词分出的 owe 承担了债务那一面。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the family built on this old verb of holding; the near-meaning group follows possession and, separately, the act of admitting.
note.cn: 形近组沿这个表示「持有」的旧动词所建的词族展开；近义组一面收「拥有」，一面收「承认」。

entries.definition: A person who owns something; own plus the person suffix -er.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有某物的人；own 加表示人的后缀 -er。

entries.definition: The state or legal right of owning something.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有某物的状态或法定权利。

entries.definition: To be in debt; it split from the same Old English verb as own.
entries.definitionCN: 欠债；与 own 由同一个古英语动词分出。

entries.definition: To have something, especially as property.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有某物，尤指作为财产。

entries.definition: To have something in your hands or under your control.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物拿在手里，或置于自己控制之下。

entries.definition: To agree that something is true, often unwillingly.
entries.definitionCN: 承认某事为真，常带不情愿的意味。

normalIntro.en: The word carries both a pointing adjective and a holding verb, and the family around it keeps turning possession into people and rights.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词同时带着一个指认的形容词和一个持有的动词，它周围的词族不断把「拥有」变成人和权利。

normal.en: Āgan in Old English meant to have; both own and owe grew from it, one as possession, the other as debt.
normal.cn: 古英语 āgan 意为持有；own 与 owe 都由它长出，一个拿拥有，一个拿欠债。

normal.en: The -er on owner marks the person, while own itself marks the thing or the act.
normal.cn: owner 上的 -er 标出人，而 own 本身标出的是东西或动作。

normal.en: Own up is possession turned inward: you take a fault and call it yours.
normal.cn: own up 是拥有向内转：你把一个过失拿过来，说它是自己的。

normal.en: On your own means you are the only person in the picture, with nobody else to lean on.
normal.cn: on your own 意味着画面里只有你一个人，没有别人可以依靠。

normal.en: A room of your own is a place the possessive word cannot share with anyone else.
normal.cn: a room of your own 是一处物主词不肯与任何人分享的地方。

abstract.en: Owning is a social fact disguised as a grammar word: it always needs someone to point at.
abstract.cn: 拥有是一个装扮成语法词的社会事实：它总要指向某个人。

abstract.en: The same word for having and for confessing hints that admitting is a way of taking responsibility as yours.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既表示拥有又表示承认，暗示坦白就是把责任认领为自己的。

abstract.en: An owner is a name attached to a thing, and the thing may outlast the name.
abstract.cn: 所有者是附在物品上的一个名字，而物品往往比名字活得更久。

examples.en: She keeps her own keys in a small tin box.
examples.cn: 她把自己的钥匙放在一个小铁盒里。

examples.en: Her family owns a small orchard outside the town.
examples.cn: 她家在城外拥有一片小果园。

examples.en: She owned that the plan had been too rushed.
examples.cn: 她承认那个计划太仓促了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧恩」——钥匙上刻着自己的名字，一喊「欧恩」就知道是自己的门。

root: 古英语 āgan（持有）的过去分词 āgen 成为形容词「自己的」，同一动词又直接发展出动词「拥有」；「欠」义则由 owe 承担。

sensesIntro.en: The core is what belongs to a particular person; the adjective points at the owner, the pronoun leaves the noun unsaid, and the verb extends to holding property and to admitting a fault.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是属于某个特定之人的东西；形容词指向主人，代词省去名词，动词则扩展到持有财产与承认过失。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a key that fits one door and no other.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把只配得上自家那扇门的钥匙。

branches.en: a name written inside a school coat
branches.cn: 校服内侧写着的名字

branches.en: a desk that nobody else may use
branches.cn: 不许别人用的那张书桌

branches.en: an orchard with a deed in a drawer
branches.cn: 抽屉里放着地契的果园

branches.en: a confession said out loud at last
branches.cn: 终于说出口的一句坦白

branches.en: a corner of a shared room marked by one chair
branches.cn: 公用房间里被一把椅子标出的角落

intro.en: Two Old English shapes meet in this word, a participle that became the adjective and a verb of holding; English suffixes then build the people and rights around it.
intro.cn: 这个词里汇合了两个古英语形态，一个成了形容词的分词，和一个表示持有的动词；英语后缀随后在它周围造出人与权利。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; its two grammatical lives both come from Old English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；它的两种语法身份都来自古英语。

items.meaningCN: 做某事或拥有某物的人

definition_zh: 物主；所有者；产权人；业主
definition_en: a person who owns something, especially the person with the legal title to property or the head of a business
core_image: 门牌上写着名字，钥匙恰好插进那把锁
scene: 老巷尽头那家旧书店换了新主人。The new owner repainted the shop front in dark green.
sceneCN: 这里 owner 是「物主、所有者」（第 1 个义项：拥有某物的人）；句意为新店主把店面刷成了深绿色。图中可辨识物件：旧书店门脸、油漆桶、刷子。

derivatives.zh: 由 owner 加 -ship 构成，指所有权、产权
由 owner 加表示「没有」的后缀 -less 构成，指无主的
由 owner 与 occupied 复合而成，指由房主自住的

senses.title: A person who owns something
senses.definition: a person who has something as property, whether a house, a car or a pet
senses.definitionCN: 把某物作为财产持有的人，可以是房子、汽车或宠物
senses.example: The owner of the little dog waited by the gate every evening.
senses.exampleCN: 那只小狗的主人每天傍晚都在门口等。
senses.why: Owner is own plus -er, the suffix that turns an action into a person, so the word names whoever holds the property.
senses.whyCN: owner 是 own 加 -er，这个后缀把动作变成人，所以这个词指持有那件财产的人。

senses.title: The person with the legal title
senses.definition: the person or company recorded in law as holding title to a property
senses.definitionCN: 在法律记录上持有某项财产所有权的人或公司
senses.example: The land owner refused to sell to the developer.
senses.exampleCN: 那位土地产权人拒绝把地卖给开发商。
senses.why: Because the verb own covers legal possession, adding -er produces the party a deed or register points to when ownership is disputed.
senses.whyCN: 既然动词 own 涵盖法律上的持有，加上 -er 就造出契据或登记簿在产权争议中指认的那一方。

senses.title: The head of a business
senses.definition: the person who runs and profits from a shop, company or sports club
senses.definitionCN: 经营一家店铺、公司或体育俱乐部并从中获利的人
senses.example: The new owner repainted the shop front in dark green.
senses.exampleCN: 新店主把店面的门脸重新刷成了深绿色。
senses.why: A business is treated as a thing that can be owned, so the same suffix names the person at the top of it, from a corner shop to a football club.
senses.whyCN: 生意被看作可以拥有的一样东西，于是同一个后缀也用来指站在它顶端的人，从街角小店到足球俱乐部都适用。

intro.en: Owner is an English formation from own and the suffix -er; no Latin ancestor is involved, and the word appears in Middle English.
intro.cn: owner 由 own 加后缀 -er 构成的英语词，不涉及拉丁语祖先，中古英语时期已经出现。

items.en: The base is āgan, to have and to hold, with its participle āgen meaning belonging to someone.
items.cn: 词基是 āgan，意为持有、拥有，其分词 āgen 意为「属于某人的」。

items.en: Middle English ownen, to possess, supplied the stem, and the agent suffix -er was added to name the person.
items.cn: 中古英语的 ownen（拥有）提供了词干，再加上表示行为者的后缀 -er 用来指人。

items.en: Forms such as ownere appear in records of land and goods, where a named person had to answer for what was held.
items.cn: ownere 这类形式出现在土地与货物的记录里，那里需要一个具名的人为所持之物负责。

items.en: With industry and property law, owner spread to shops, ships and companies, and compounds such as landowner became common.
items.cn: 随着工业与财产法的发展，owner 扩展到店铺、船只和公司，landowner 之类的复合词也变得常见。

items.en: Modern English uses owner for people and ownership for the abstract right, keeping the two endings clearly apart.
items.cn: 现代英语用 owner 指人，用 ownership 指抽象的权利，两个后缀分工清楚。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the base word and the suffixes that rebuild it; the near-meaning group gathers other names for the person who holds property.
note.cn: 形近组沿基础词和重建它的后缀展开；近义组收其他指「持有财产之人」的说法。

entries.definition: To have something as property, or belonging to oneself.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有某物，或指属于自己的。

entries.definition: The legal right or state of owning something.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有某物的法定权利或状态。

entries.definition: A person who owns land.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有土地的人。

entries.definition: The owner of a business or property.
entries.definitionCN: 企业或房产的所有者。

entries.definition: A person who has something in their possession.
entries.definitionCN: 占有某物的人。

entries.definition: A person who owns a house or land and rents it out.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有房屋或土地并出租的人。

normalIntro.en: The word adds one suffix to a verb of holding, and everything else in the family simply adds another suffix to that person.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词只是给表示持有的动词加了一个后缀，词族里其余的词又在这个「人」上继续加后缀。

normal.en: Owner is own plus -er: the suffix does nothing but turn holding into a person.
normal.cn: owner 是 own 加 -er：这个后缀只做一件事，把持有变成人。

normal.en: Ownership adds -ship to owner and turns the person back into an abstract right.
normal.cn: ownership 在 owner 后加 -ship，又把人变回一种抽象权利。

normal.en: Landowner and homeowner simply put the kind of property in front of the person.
normal.cn: landowner 与 homeowner 只是把财产种类放在人前面。

normal.en: The owner of a shop and the owner of a dog share one word because both answer for something.
normal.cn: 店主和狗主人共用一个词，因为两者都要为某样东西负责。

normal.en: Owe, own and owner all come from the same Old English verb of holding.
normal.cn: owe、own 与 owner 都来自同一个表示持有的古英语动词。

abstract.en: A person's name on a deed is a way of making a claim visible to everyone else.
abstract.cn: 地契上写下一个人的名字，是把一份主张变得人人可见的方法。

abstract.en: Ownership can be sold, lent or fought over, while the owner may change many times.
abstract.cn: 所有权可以被出售、出借或争夺，而所有者可能换了许多次。

abstract.en: Every owner is also someone who answers for what happens to the thing owned.
abstract.cn: 每个所有者同时也是那个要为所拥有之物的遭遇负责的人。

examples.en: The owner of the little dog waited by the gate every evening.
examples.cn: 那只小狗的主人每天傍晚都在门口等。

examples.en: The land owner refused to sell to the developer.
examples.cn: 那位土地产权人拒绝把地卖给开发商。

examples.en: The new owner repainted the shop front in dark green.
examples.cn: 新店主把店面的门脸重新刷成了深绿色。

scene: 快递站的塑料筐里堆着大小不一的纸箱，店员用胶带把最后一个封好。The clerk handed her a heavy package wrapped in brown paper.
sceneCN: 这里的 package 是「包裹」（第 1 个义项：包装好待寄送的东西）；句意为店员递给她一个用牛皮纸包好的沉包裹。图中可辨识物件：塑料筐、纸箱、胶带。

senses.title: Something wrapped for sending or selling
senses.definition: something wrapped in paper, plastic or a box so that it can be carried, sent or sold
senses.definitionCN: 用纸、塑料或盒子包好，便于携带、寄送或出售的东西
senses.example: The clerk handed her a heavy package wrapped in brown paper.
senses.exampleCN: 店员递给她一个用牛皮纸包好的沉包裹。
senses.why: Package is pack plus the French ending -age, which names an action and its result, so the word means the outcome of packing: a thing tied up and sealed.
senses.whyCN: package 是 pack 加法语词尾 -age，这个后缀表示动作及其结果，所以这个词指「打包」的产物：一个被捆好、封好的东西。

senses.title: A set of things offered as one deal
senses.definition: several things, proposals or services put together and offered as a single whole
senses.definitionCN: 把若干东西、提议或服务合在一起，作为一个整体提供
senses.example: The government announced a package of measures to help small firms.
senses.exampleCN: 政府公布了一揽子帮助小企业的措施。
senses.why: If one wrapper can hold several objects, the same noun can hold several proposals under one agreement, which is how the word reached politics, tourism and software.
senses.whyCN: 既然一层包装能装下好几样东西，同一个名词就能把好几项提议装进一份协议里，这个词就是这样走进了政治、旅游与软件。

senses.title: To wrap goods for sale or sending
senses.definition: to put goods into a wrapper or a container, especially in a form suitable for selling
senses.definitionCN: 把货物装进包装物或容器，尤指做成适合出售的样子
senses.example: They packaged the biscuits in small foil bags.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把饼干装进小小的锡纸袋里。
senses.why: The verb reverses the noun: instead of naming the thing already packed, it names the act of packing it, and modern marketing stretched it to designing the wrapper as well.
senses.whyCN: 动词把这个名词翻了个面：不再指已经包好的东西，而指把它包起来这个动作；现代营销又把它扩展到包装的设计本身。

intro.en: Package is an English formation of the sixteenth century, made from the old noun pack and the French ending -age; the root pack is usually traced to Middle Dutch or Middle Low German, so the word is Germanic rather than Latin.
intro.cn: package 是十六世纪英语自造的派生词，由古老名词 pack 与法语词尾 -age 构成；词根 pack 一般认为来自中古荷兰语或中古低地德语，因此这族词属日耳曼语而非拉丁语。

items.en: The noun pak meant a bundle tied up for carrying, and it is the usual source given for the English word pack.
items.cn: 名词 pak 指捆好便于搬运的包裹，通常被认为是英语 pack 的来源。

items.en: English took the noun as pack, a bundle or a load, and used it for goods tied together for a journey or a market.
items.cn: 英语把这个名词收作 pack，意为捆、一捆货，用来指为出行或赶集而捆在一起的货物。

items.en: The ending -age came into English through French from Latin -aticum and named an action or its result, as in voyage and baggage.
items.cn: 词尾 -age 经法语从拉丁语 -aticum 进入英语，表示动作或其结果，如 voyage 与 baggage。

items.en: Package first named both the act of packing and the bundle that resulted, and it soon covered goods prepared for a customer.
items.cn: package 最早同时指打包这个动作和打好的包，不久便用来指为顾客备好的货品。

items.en: Modern English adds package deal and package tour in trade and travel, the software package in computing, and the verb to package.
items.cn: 现代英语在商贸与旅游中加上 package deal 与 package tour，在计算机领域加上 software package，还发展出动词用法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on pack or on the same -age pattern; the near-meaning group collects words for wrapped goods and for bundles.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在 pack 上或采用同一 -age 模式的词；近义组收表示包好的货物与捆扎之物的词。

normal.en: A packet is the small cousin: both words grew from pack, but a packet is a little paper or plastic container, while a package can be as big as a carton.

normal.cn: package deal 借用了包裹的画面：几样东西捆在一起，当作一件来卖。

normal.en: The verb adds nothing except the act, so packaged goods are simply goods that have been put into their wrappers.
normal.cn: 动词只添上动作本身，所以 packaged goods 不过是已经装进包装的货物。

normal.en: British speakers often say parcel for something sent by post, while package is the usual word in American English.

abstract.en: A package deal hides its seams: the wrapping makes several separate things look like one decision.
abstract.cn: 一揽子交易藏起了接缝：包装让几件彼此独立的事看起来像同一个决定。

abstract.en: Wrapping protects a thing and also hides it, which is why the same word can mean care and concealment.

senses.example: She dog-eared the page to mark her place.
senses.exampleCN: 她把那一页折了个角，标住自己读到哪儿。
senses.why: Latin pagina named the column of writing on a papyrus sheet, so the word began as the surface that carries text rather than the sheet itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pagina 本指纸草上书写的一栏文字，所以这个词最初指承载文字的那一面，而不是整张纸。

senses.title: A screen of content on a website
senses.definition: a single screen of content that a browser loads from a website
senses.definitionCN: 浏览器从网站载入的一屏内容
senses.example: The error page told us the link had expired.
senses.exampleCN: 那个错误页面提示我们链接已经失效。
senses.why: When text moved from paper to glass, the old word for a readable surface was simply carried over to what a browser shows.
senses.whyCN: 文字从纸面搬到玻璃屏上之后，人们就把这个表示「可读表面」的旧词直接搬去指浏览器显示的内容。

senses.title: To call a name out over a speaker
senses.definition: to call someone's name through a loudspeaker or an electronic device in order to reach them
senses.definitionCN: 通过扩音器或电子设备呼叫某人的名字，以便找到对方
senses.example: The airport staff paged her twice before she heard it.
senses.exampleCN: 机场工作人员呼叫了她两次，她才听见。
senses.why: This sense is usually said to come from the page who ran messages in a household; sending a name out to find a person survived after the servant vanished.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项一般认为来自旧时在宅院里跑腿传话的侍童；侍童消失了，但「把名字传出去找人」的做法留了下来。

senses.title: To look through a book page by page
senses.definition: to turn the pages of a book or magazine quickly while looking at them
senses.definitionCN: 快速翻动书或杂志的页面，一边翻一边看
senses.example: He paged through the atlas while waiting.
senses.exampleCN: 他等的时候一页页翻着那本地图册。
senses.why: The verb only turns the noun into an action: if a page is the unit of a book, then to page is to move through those units.
senses.whyCN: 动词只是把名词变成动作：既然页是书的单位，那么翻页就是沿着这些单位一路往下走。

intro.en: Page goes back to a Latin noun for a column of writing, and English later used the same word for servants, web screens and loudspeaker calls.
intro.cn: page 可追到拉丁语中表示「书写的一栏」的名词，英语后来用同一个词指侍从、网页和广播呼叫。

items.en: Pagina meant a column of writing on a papyrus roll, and it is generally thought to come from the verb pangere.
items.cn: pagina 指纸草卷上的一栏文字，一般认为出自动词 pangere。

items.en: Pangere meant to fasten or plant, and the link to writing is usually explained as lines fixed onto a surface.
items.cn: pangere 意为固定、插下；它与书写的联系，一般认为是指一行行字被「固定」在表面上。

items.en: Old French page named both a leaf of a book and a young servant, and English took over both meanings.
items.cn: 古法语 page 既指书的一页，也指年轻的侍从，英语把这两个意思都接了过来。

items.en: Middle English page kept the book sense and the servant sense side by side for centuries.
items.cn: 中古英语的 page 让「书页」和「侍从」两个意思并行了好几百年。

items.en: Modern English added the newspaper page, the web page, and the verbs for calling a name and turning pages.
items.cn: 现代英语又添上报纸版面、网页，以及「呼叫名字」和「翻页」的动词用法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built on the Latin stem for a written column; the near-meaning group collects words for paper leaves and for calling someone.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在「书写的一栏」这一拉丁词干上的形式；近义组收表示纸页和呼唤某人的词。

entries.definition: The Latin noun for a column of writing, the source of the English word.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语中表示书写栏目的名词，是英语这个词的来源。

entries.definition: To number the pages of a document.
entries.definitionCN: 给文件的各页编上页码。

entries.definition: A small device that beeps when someone is trying to reach you.
entries.definitionCN: 有人找你时会响的小型设备；寻呼机。

entries.definition: A public show with costumes and scenes; it is only close in spelling, and its source is different.
entries.definitionCN: 有服装和场景的公开演出；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A single piece of paper, or one side of it.
entries.definitionCN: 一张纸，或纸的一面。

entries.definition: A sheet of paper in a book, especially when numbered on both sides.
entries.definitionCN: 书中一张纸，尤指两面都编了号的。

entries.definition: What a device shows at one time.
entries.definitionCN: 设备一次显示的内容；屏幕。

entries.definition: To call someone to come, often officially.
entries.definitionCN: 召唤某人前来，常带正式意味。

normalIntro.en: Page began as the written surface of a roll, and its family keeps two ideas alive: numbered leaves and calling a name out.
normalIntro.cn: page 最初指卷轴上书写的那一面，同族词一直保有两个想法：编了号的纸页，以及把名字喊出去。

normal.en: Latin pagina is the written column, so page is first a surface that holds text.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 pagina 是书写的一栏，所以 page 首先是承载文字的表面。

normal.en: Pangere means to fasten, which is why pagina is often explained as lines fixed onto a surface.
normal.cn: pangere 意为固定，所以一般认为 pagina 就是被固定在表面上的一行行字。

normal.en: The suffix -ate in paginate turns the noun into a verb: to give a document its page numbers.
normal.cn: paginate 里的后缀 -ate 把名词变成动词，意思是给文件编上页码。

normal.en: The servant sense survives in the verb to page someone, because a page carried messages by name.
normal.cn: 「侍从」这个意思留在动词 to page 里，因为侍从就是按名字替人传话的。

normal.en: Web page puts the old word on a new surface, so the meaning moves from paper to screen without changing its core.
normal.cn: 网页只是把这个旧词放到新的表面上，词义从纸移到屏幕，核心并没有变。

abstract.en: A page is a unit small enough to finish, which is why turning the page can mean starting over.
abstract.cn: 一页小到能读完，所以「翻过这一页」也可以表示重新开始。

abstract.en: Numbering pages makes a book addressable: any sentence can be found again later.
abstract.cn: 给页编号让整本书可以被定位：任何一句话以后都能重新找到。

abstract.en: One word covers paper, screens and loudspeaker calls because all three put a name or a text where someone can meet it.
abstract.cn: 同一个词覆盖纸、屏幕和广播，因为这三者都是把名字或文字放到别人能遇上的地方。

examples.en: He turned the page and found a note in the margin.
examples.cn: 他翻过这一页，在页边发现一行批注。

examples.en: The site's help page explains how to reset the password.
examples.cn: 网站的帮助页面说明了如何重设密码。

examples.en: The nurse paged the doctor at midnight.
examples.cn: 护士在午夜呼叫了医生。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佩奇」——翻开书页，小猪佩奇正坐在页码上；page 是书页，也是呼叫。

root: 拉丁语 pagina（书写的一栏）一般认为出自 pangere（固定、钉住），经古法语 page 进入英语；同族词多与纸页、编号有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core image is a written surface you can turn; from it come the book page, the web page, the act of turning pages, and the call that sends a name out.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心意象是一面可以翻动的书写表面；书页、网页、翻页的动作，以及把名字喊出去的呼叫，都由此展开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the corner of a page lifting in a breeze, showing the line above it.
core.cn: 核心意象：书页一角被风掀起，露出上一行还没读完的字。

branches.en: a reader folding a corner to keep the place
branches.cn: 读者折起页角记住读到哪儿

branches.en: a browser showing the same old word on glass
branches.cn: 浏览器把同一个旧词显示在玻璃屏上

branches.en: a thumb moving quickly along the edge of a magazine
branches.cn: 拇指沿着杂志边缘快速翻动

branches.en: a voice repeating a name through a ceiling speaker
branches.cn: 声音通过天花板上的喇叭重复一个名字

branches.en: a paperless notice that still calls itself a page
branches.cn: 一份没有纸的通知仍然自称页面

intro.en: The word rests on the Latin noun pagina and the verb pangere, with English endings that produce a device and a numbering verb.
intro.cn: 这个词依托拉丁名词 pagina 与动词 pangere，再加上英语词尾，生出设备名和表示编号的动词。

latinIntro.en: Pagina, the Latin noun for a column of writing, and pangere, the verb to fasten, stand behind the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语名词 pagina（书写的一栏）与动词 pangere（固定）是英语这个词背后的来源。
