a leaf of a book; a young servant

derivatives.zh: 由 page 加 -er 构成，指寻呼机
由 paginate 加 -ion 构成，指页码编排
由 page 与 turner 复合而成，指让人一口气读完的书

definition_zh: 疼痛；痛苦；辛劳；使痛苦
definition_en: the feeling of physical hurt, deep emotional suffering, or the effort and trouble that something costs
core_image: 一只手按住肋侧，眉头因为一阵刺痛而皱起
scene: 雨夜里，老人扶着墙慢慢坐下，手掌一直按着膝盖。The pain in his knee kept him awake until dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 pain 是「身体的疼痛」（第 1 个义项：生理上的痛感）；句意是膝盖的疼痛让他一直醒到天亮。图中可辨识的物件：夜雨、墙、老人按住膝盖的手。

collocations.zh: 成长中的烦恼；发展初期的阵痛

derivatives.zh: 由 pain 加形容词后缀 -ful 构成，义为「令人疼痛的；痛苦的」
由 pain 加表示「没有」的后缀 -less 构成，义为「无痛的」
由 pain 与 killer 复合而成，义为「止痛药」
由 pain 加 -ed 构成，义为「显出痛苦的」

senses.title: Physical hurt in the body
senses.definition: an unpleasant feeling in the body caused by injury or illness
senses.definitionCN: 由受伤或疾病引起的身体上的不适感觉
senses.example: The pain in his knee kept him awake until dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 膝盖的疼痛让他一直醒到天亮。
senses.why: Latin poena meant a penalty, so the word starts from something imposed on a person rather than chosen; bodily hurt is felt as a price.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 poena 意为「惩罚」，所以这个词的起点是加在人身上的东西，而不是自己挑的；身体的痛就像被收走的一笔代价。

senses.title: Deep emotional suffering
senses.definition: a feeling of great sadness or distress that is not caused by physical injury
senses.definitionCN: 并非由身体损伤引起、而是源于内心的巨大悲伤或难受
senses.example: The pain of losing her friend never fully left her.
senses.exampleCN: 失去朋友的痛苦始终没有完全离开她。
senses.why: If pain is a penalty paid, it can also be paid in the mind, so the same word covers grief that leaves no visible wound.
senses.whyCN: 既然 pain 是一笔要付的代价，也就可以在心里付；于是同一个词也覆盖了看不见伤口的悲伤。

senses.title: Effort and trouble taken
senses.definition: the effort and careful work that someone puts into doing something properly, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 为把事情做好而付出的努力与细心，通常用复数
senses.example: She took great pains to hide the crack in the vase.
senses.exampleCN: 她费了好大功夫才把花瓶上的裂缝藏住。
senses.why: Anything worth doing exactly right costs some discomfort, so the plural pains came to mean the trouble one is willing to spend.
senses.whyCN: 凡是要做到位的事都得付点不舒服的代价，于是复数 pains 转而指人愿意花出去的那份心力。

senses.title: To cause someone hurt or distress
senses.definition: to make someone feel physical or emotional hurt
senses.definitionCN: 使某人感到身体上或情绪上的难受
senses.example: It pained him to admit that he had been wrong.
senses.exampleCN: 承认自己错了让他很难受。
senses.why: The noun became a verb by reversing the direction: instead of feeling the penalty, a person or event now imposes it on someone.
senses.whyCN: 名词转成动词时方向反了过来：不再是承受那份惩罚，而是某人或某事把它加到别人身上。

intro.en: Pain goes back to a Latin word for penalty, which reached English through French and slowly moved from punishment to the hurt a body or mind feels.
intro.cn: pain 可追到拉丁语中表示「惩罚」的词，经法语进入英语，词义从处罚慢慢移到身体或心里感到的痛。

items.en: Poena meant penalty, punishment, or the price paid for a wrong.
items.cn: poena 意为处罚、惩罚，或为过错付出的代价。

items.en: The adjective poenalis described what belongs to punishment, and it survives in English penal.
items.cn: 形容词 poenalis 描述与惩罚有关的东西，在英语中留下 penal 一词。

items.en: Old French peine took over the sense of punishment and also of hardship and suffering.
items.cn: 古法语 peine 承接了「惩罚」，也带上「艰苦、受苦」的意思。

items.en: Middle English pain named both the penalty and the bodily hurt, and the bodily sense gradually became the main one.
items.cn: 中古英语的 pain 既指惩罚也指身体的伤痛，后来身体上的痛感渐渐成了主要意思。

items.en: Modern English keeps the physical sense, adds the emotional one, and keeps the plural as a word for effort.
items.cn: 现代英语保留身体痛感，添上情绪上的痛苦，并让复数形式表示付出的辛劳。

note.en: The look-alike group collects legal relatives of the Latin word for penalty; the near-meaning group collects words for hurt and suffering.
note.cn: 形近组收源自「惩罚」这一拉丁词的司法同族词；近义组收表示伤痛与受苦的词。

entries.definition: The Latin noun for penalty, the source of the English word.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语中表示惩罚的名词，是英语这个词的来源。

entries.definition: Relating to punishment by law.
entries.definitionCN: 与法律上的惩罚有关的。

entries.definition: A punishment for breaking a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 因违反规则而受到的处罚。

entries.definition: To long for something sadly; it is only close in spelling, and its source is different.
entries.definitionCN: 苦苦思念；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A continuous dull pain.
entries.definitionCN: 持续而隐约的疼痛。

entries.definition: The state of being tender and painful to touch.
entries.definitionCN: 一碰就疼的状态。

entries.definition: Serious pain of body or mind that lasts.
entries.definitionCN: 持续的身体或精神痛苦。

entries.definition: Extreme worry, sadness or discomfort.
entries.definitionCN: 极度的忧虑、悲伤或不适。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a Latin noun for penalty, and its family runs from legal punishment to bodily hurt and the effort people spend.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在表示「惩罚」的拉丁名词上，同族词从法律处罚一路延伸到身体的痛和人们肯花的力气。

normal.en: Latin poena is a penalty, so pain is something charged to you rather than something you choose.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 poena 是惩罚，所以 pain 是被记在你账上的东西，而不是你自己挑的。

normal.en: Penal and penalty keep the legal side of poena visible in modern English.
normal.cn: penal 和 penalty 让 poena 的司法一面在现代英语里仍然看得见。

normal.en: The suffix -ful in painful adds fullness: a thing that is full of pain.
normal.cn: painful 里的后缀 -ful 添上「满」的意思：一件装满疼痛的东西。

normal.en: The suffix -less in painless removes it: a state with no pain at all.
normal.cn: painless 里的后缀 -less 把它去掉：完全没有疼痛的状态。

normal.en: Take pains is the old idea of paying a price, now spent as careful effort.
normal.cn: take pains 原本是「付出代价」的老想法，如今花出去的是细致的用心。

abstract.en: A word that once meant a fine now means a hurt, which suggests we treat pain as something the body pays.
abstract.cn: 一个曾经表示罚款的词如今表示疼痛，说明我们把痛当成身体付出的东西。

abstract.en: Pain is the body's way of charging attention to a place that needs care.
abstract.cn: 疼痛是身体把注意力记到某个需要照料的地方。

abstract.en: The plural pains reminds us that careful work also has a cost, just a quieter one.
abstract.cn: 复数 pains 提醒人：细心的活儿也有代价，只是安静一些。

examples.en: The pain in his knee kept him awake until dawn.
examples.cn: 膝盖的疼痛让他一直醒到天亮。

examples.en: The pain of losing her friend never fully left her.
examples.cn: 失去朋友的痛苦始终没有完全离开她。

examples.en: It pained him to admit that he had been wrong.
examples.cn: 承认自己错了让他很难受。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佩恩」——佩恩磕到桌角，疼得直吸凉气；pain 就是疼痛。

root: 拉丁语 poena（惩罚、代价）经古法语 peine 进入英语；一般认为词义由「受罚」转到「受苦、疼痛」，同族词多与处罚、痛感有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core image is a hurt that costs you something; the senses divide into bodily pain, grief of the mind, the effort one pays out, and the act of hurting someone.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心意象是一种要你付出代价的痛；义项分为身体的痛、心里的苦、肯付出去的辛劳，以及让别人难受的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pressed to the ribs while a sharp ache narrows the eyes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手按住肋侧，一阵刺痛让眉头皱起。

branches.en: a hand pressed hard against a sore knee
branches.cn: 一只手紧紧按住发疼的膝盖

branches.en: an empty chair that still hurts to look at
branches.cn: 一把看一眼就难受的空椅子

branches.en: a careful hand hiding a crack in a vase
branches.cn: 一只手小心地把花瓶裂缝遮住

branches.en: a face that has just heard its own mistake named
branches.cn: 刚听到自己错误被点破的一张脸

branches.en: one word holding a wound and a grief together
branches.cn: 同一个词同时装着伤口和悲伤

intro.en: The word is carried by a Latin noun of penalty, its adjective, and two English suffixes that add or remove pain.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示惩罚的拉丁名词、它的形容词，以及两个给「痛」添上或去掉的后缀共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Poena, the Latin noun for penalty, and its adjective poenalis stand behind the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语名词 poena（惩罚）及其形容词 poenalis 是英语这个词背后的来源。

derivatives.zh: 由 pain 加 -ful 构成，指令人疼痛的

definition_zh: 疼痛的；令人痛苦的；艰难的；令人尴尬的
definition_en: causing physical hurt, deeply upsetting, or difficult and unpleasant to go through
core_image: 手指碰到还没长好的伤口，整个人一缩
scene: 换药的时候，纱布刚碰到伤口，病人就绷紧了肩膀。The dressing was changed slowly because the wound was still painful.
sceneCN: 这里 painful 是「疼痛的、碰着就疼的」（第 1 个义项：引起身体疼痛的）；句意是伤口还疼，所以换药换得很慢。图中可辨识的物件：纱布、伤口、绷紧的肩膀。

pos.zh: 疼痛的；令人痛苦的；艰难的；令人尴尬的

derivatives.zh: 由 painful 加 -ly 构成，义为「痛苦地；费力地」
由 painful 加 -ness 构成，义为「痛苦；难受」
去掉形容词后缀 -ful 得到的基础名词，义为「疼痛；痛苦」
由 pain 加 -less 构成，义为「无痛的」

senses.title: Causing physical hurt
senses.definition: causing a feeling of hurt in the body
senses.definitionCN: 引起身体痛感的
senses.example: The wound was still painful when the dressing was changed.
senses.exampleCN: 换药时伤口还在疼。
senses.why: The suffix -ful means full of, so painful describes something full of pain, a thing that gives pain rather than feels it.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ful 表示「充满」，所以 painful 形容某物充满疼痛，是「给出疼痛」而不是「感到疼痛」。

senses.title: Causing deep sadness
senses.definition: making someone feel great sadness or distress
senses.definitionCN: 使人感到巨大悲伤或难受的
senses.example: It was a painful reminder of how much she had lost.
senses.exampleCN: 那是一个令人痛苦的提醒，让她想起自己失去了多少。
senses.why: If a thing can be full of bodily pain, it can also be full of grief, so the word moves from flesh to feeling without changing shape.
senses.whyCN: 既然一个东西能装满身体的痛，也能装满悲伤，于是这个词从皮肉移到情绪，形式却一点没变。

senses.title: Hard to get through
senses.definition: difficult, tiring or unpleasant to experience or perform
senses.definitionCN: 经历或执行起来困难、累人或难受的
senses.example: The first year of the project was a painful process.
senses.exampleCN: 项目的第一年是个艰难的过程。
senses.why: Anything that takes effort feels like a small injury to comfort, which is why painful stretches to mean laborious rather than literally sore.
senses.whyCN: 凡是费力的事都像对舒适的一次小损伤，所以 painful 会引申为「艰难、费力」，而不是字面意义上的「疼」。

senses.title: Awkward and embarrassing
senses.definition: so awkward that people feel uncomfortable and do not know what to say
senses.definitionCN: 尴尬到让人不自在、不知道该说什么的
senses.example: A painful silence followed his question.
senses.exampleCN: 他问完之后是一阵令人尴尬的沉默。
senses.why: Embarrassment is felt as a sting, and English often borrows the language of physical hurt for social discomfort.
senses.whyCN: 尴尬会被感受成一种刺痛，英语常用身体的痛来形容社交上的不适。

intro.en: Painful is an English construction on pain, and pain itself came from a Latin word for penalty through French.
intro.cn: painful 是在 pain 上构成的英语词，而 pain 本身来自拉丁语中表示惩罚的词，经法语传来。

items.en: Poena meant penalty or the price paid for a wrong, and it did not yet name a bodily sensation.
items.cn: poena 意为处罚，或为过错付出的代价，当时还不指身体的感觉。

items.en: Old French peine carried both punishment and hardship into the sense of suffering.
items.cn: 古法语 peine 把「惩罚」和「艰苦」一起带进了「受苦」的意思。

items.en: Middle English pain settled on the hurt a person feels in body or mind.
items.cn: 中古英语的 pain 定在人在身体或心里感到的痛。

items.en: The suffix -ful, from a word meaning full, was added to nouns to mean full of or causing.
items.cn: 后缀 -ful 来自意为「满」的词，加在名词后表示「充满」或「引起」。

items.en: Modern English uses painful for sore wounds, sad news, hard years and awkward quiet alike.
items.cn: 现代英语用 painful 同时形容发疼的伤口、令人难过的消息、艰难的岁月和尴尬的安静。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built on pain with other endings; the near-meaning group collects adjectives for soreness and distress.
note.cn: 形近组收 pain 接其他词尾构成的形式；近义组收表示酸痛与难受的形容词。

normalIntro.en: Painful is pain plus a suffix that says full of, so every sense asks what kind of pain a thing is full of.
normalIntro.cn: painful 是 pain 加上表示「充满」的后缀，所以每个义项都在问：这个东西装的是哪一种痛。

normal.en: The suffix -ful means full of, so painful names the source of pain while pain names the feeling.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ful 意为充满，所以 painful 指痛的来源，pain 则指痛的感觉。

normal.en: Painless swaps -ful for -less, and the meaning turns to its opposite.
normal.cn: painless 把 -ful 换成 -less，意思就翻到反面。

normal.en: Painfully adds -ly and describes how something is done.
normal.cn: painfully 再加 -ly，描述一件事是以什么方式做的。

normal.en: A painful process hurts without wounding, which shows how far the suffix can stretch.
normal.cn: 艰难的过程并不造成伤口却让人难受，可见这个后缀能伸多远。

normal.en: The base pain came from Latin poena, a penalty, so the family always carries the idea of a cost.
normal.cn: 基础词 pain 来自拉丁语 poena（惩罚），所以这一族词总带着「代价」的想法。

abstract.en: English lets a suffix decide direction: painful is what gives pain, not what feels it.
abstract.cn: 英语让后缀决定方向：painful 是「给出痛」的东西，而不是「感到痛」的。

abstract.en: Calling a silence painful says that embarrassment is a kind of injury we all recognise.
abstract.cn: 把沉默叫作 painful，等于说尴尬是一种人人都认得的损伤。

abstract.en: A word for penalty became a word for hurt, and then a word for anything hard to endure.
abstract.cn: 一个表示惩罚的词先变成「痛」，再变成「任何难以忍受的事」。

examples.cn: 换药时伤口还在疼。

definition_zh: 一双；一对；一对人；一对动物；配对
definition_en: two things or people that belong together, or to put two such things together
core_image: 两只一模一样的手套并排放着，指尖对着指尖
scene: 清晨的门口，两只沾了泥的靴子被人并排放好，鞋尖朝外。She could not find the pair of gloves that matched her coat.
sceneCN: 这里 pair 是「一双、一对配套的东西」（第 1 个义项：成对使用的两件物品）；句意是她找不到和外套相配的那副手套。图中可辨识的物件：门口的靴子、泥点、手套。

senses.title: Two things that go together
senses.definition: two things of the same kind that are used together or look the same
senses.definitionCN: 同一种类、搭配使用或看起来相配的两件东西
senses.example: She could not find the pair of gloves that matched her coat.
senses.exampleCN: 她找不到和外套相配的那副手套。
senses.why: Latin paria were equal things, so the word starts from two items that answer each other, not from any particular object.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 paria 指「相等的东西」，所以这个词的起点是两件彼此对应的物品，而不是某种特定的东西。

senses.title: Two people linked together
senses.definition: two people who are connected by love, work or a shared activity
senses.definitionCN: 因感情、工作或共同活动而连在一起的两个人
senses.example: The pair have worked in the same lab for ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个人在同一间实验室共事了十年。
senses.why: Since paria means equals, the word easily moves from matching objects to two people who are matched in some role.
senses.whyCN: 既然 paria 意为「相等之物」，这个词就很容易从相配的物品转到在某种角色上相配的两个人。

senses.title: Two animals kept together
senses.definition: a male and a female animal, or two animals of the same kind, kept together
senses.definitionCN: 养在一起的一雌一雄，或同种的两只动物
senses.example: The farm bought a pair of geese for the pond.
senses.exampleCN: 农场为池塘买了一对鹅。
senses.why: Breeding needs two, and the old sense of equal things fits a male and female kept together for mating.
senses.whyCN: 繁殖需要两个，而「相等之物」的老义正好贴合为交配而养在一起的一雄一雌。

senses.title: To put two things together
senses.definition: to join two things or people so that they form a matching set or a working team
senses.definitionCN: 把两件东西或两个人组合起来，成为相配的一套或一个搭档
senses.example: Students were paired by level for the speaking test.
senses.exampleCN: 口语考试按水平把学生两人一组配对。
senses.why: Once a pair names a set of two, the verb simply performs the action of making that set exist.
senses.whyCN: 既然 pair 指「两个组成的一套」，动词就是让这样一套真正形成的动作。

intro.en: Pair comes from Latin words for equal things, which passed through French and came to name any two items that answer each other.
intro.cn: pair 来自拉丁语中表示「相等之物」的词，经法语传来，后来指任何彼此对应的两件东西。

items.en: Par meant equal or a match, and it is the stem behind a family of words about being level.
items.cn: par 意为相等的、对等的，是整族表示「持平」的词背后的词干。

items.en: The neuter plural paria named equal things taken together, which is the form the noun needed.
items.cn: 中性复数 paria 指放在一起的相等之物，正好是名词所需的形式。

items.en: Old French paire kept the sense of a set of two matching things.
items.cn: 古法语 paire 保留了「相配的两件成一套」的意思。

items.en: Middle English pair widened from matching objects to couples, partners and animals kept together.
items.cn: 中古英语的 pair 从相配的物品扩展到伴侣、搭档和养在一起的动物。

items.en: Modern English uses pair as a noun for any matched two and as a verb for the act of matching.
items.cn: 现代英语把 pair 用作名词指任何相配的两个，也用作动词指配对的动作。

note.cn: 形近组收「相等」这一拉丁词干的同族词；近义组收表示「两个」与「搭档」的词。

normalIntro.en: Pair rests on a Latin word for equal, so the whole family is about two things that stand level with each other.
normalIntro.cn: pair 依托拉丁语中表示「相等」的词，所以整族词都围绕「彼此持平的两样东西」。

normal.en: Latin par means equal, and paria is its plural for equal things, which is exactly what a pair is.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 par 意为相等，paria 是它的复数，指相等之物，正是一对的意思。

normal.en: Parity, par and compare all keep the equal part of the same stem.
normal.cn: parity、par 和 compare 都保留着同一词干里「相等」的那部分。

normal.en: Pair up adds a particle that turns the noun into the action of forming a set.
normal.cn: pair up 加上一个小词，就把名词变成「组成一套」的动作。

normal.en: In pairs uses the plural to mean two at a time, a pattern that appears in classrooms and queues.
normal.cn: in pairs 用复数表示「一次两个」，课堂和排队时都常见。

normal.en: A pair of shoes works because the two shoes answer each other, not because there are simply two shoes.
normal.cn: 一双鞋之所以成双，是因为两只鞋彼此对应，而不是因为刚好有两只鞋。

abstract.en: Two equal things need each other to be a pair, which is why the word carries a quiet idea of balance.
abstract.cn: 两个相等之物要彼此依存才成对，所以这个词暗暗带着平衡的意味。

abstract.en: Pairing is a way of organising the world by twos, from shoes to lab partners.
abstract.cn: 配对是把世界按「两个」来整理的一种方式，从鞋子到实验搭档都一样。

abstract.en: A word born from equality reminds us that a pair only works when both sides count.
abstract.cn: 一个从「相等」生出的词提醒人：一对要成立，两边都得算数。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佩尔」——把两只配好，正好配成一对；pair 是一双。

root: 拉丁语 par（相等的）之中性复数 paria 指「相等之物」，经古法语 paire 进入英语；同族词多与「相等、对等」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is two things standing equal to each other; the senses spread to objects used together, linked people, animals kept as a pair, and the act of matching.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是彼此持平的两样东西；义项扩展到配套使用的物品、连在一起的两个人、成对饲养的动物，以及配对的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two identical gloves laid side by side, fingertip to fingertip.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只一模一样的手套并排放着，指尖对着指尖。

branches.en: two shoes waiting at the door toe to toe
branches.cn: 两只鞋并排等在门口，鞋尖对着鞋尖

branches.en: two lab partners sharing one bench
branches.cn: 两个实验搭档共用一张台子

branches.en: a goose following its mate to the pond
branches.cn: 一只鹅跟着伴侣走向池塘

branches.en: names on a list being joined two by two
branches.cn: 名单上的名字被两个两个连起来

branches.en: a word for equality used for gloves and for people
branches.cn: 一个表示相等的词，既用于手套也用于人

intro.en: The word grows from a Latin stem for equal, its plural form, and English endings that turn it into an adjective, a noun and a verb.
intro.cn: 这个词从表示「相等」的拉丁词干和它的复数形式生长出来，再加上英语词尾，变成形容词、名词和动词。

latinIntro.en: Par, the Latin adjective for equal, and its neuter plural paria stand behind the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语形容词 par（相等的）及其中性复数 paria 是英语这个词背后的来源。

derivatives.zh: 由 pair 加 -ed 构成，指成对的
由 pair 加 -ing 构成，指配对
由 un- 与 paired 构成，指未配对的

definition_zh: 宫殿；王宫；主教府；豪华宅邸；大型公共文化建筑
definition_en: the official residence of a king, queen, bishop or other high dignitary, or any very large and grand building
core_image: 一道正门通向铺石大院，院后是层层抬高的殿堂，每一层都比前一层更不容外人进入
scene: 铁门后是铺石大院，台阶一层层通向正殿。The palace opens its state rooms to visitors only two months a year.
sceneCN: 这里 palace 指「君主或高级显要的官邸」（第 1 个义项：王宫、宫殿）；句意为这座王宫每年只有两个月向访客开放国事厅。图中可辨识物件：铁门、铺石大院、台阶、正殿；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 豪华大宅；大型公共建筑

derivatives.zh: 宫殿般的；宏伟的
行宫领地；普法尔茨伯爵领地
宫廷政变
宫廷革命
意大利式府邸

senses.title: The residence of a ruler
senses.definition: the official home and ceremonial centre of a king, queen or emperor
senses.definitionCN: 国王、女王或皇帝的官邸与礼仪中心
senses.example: The palace balcony faces the wide avenue where crowds gather.
senses.exampleCN: 王宫的阳台朝向人群聚集的宽阔大道。
senses.why: the word began as the name of one hill in Rome, then of the emperor's house on it, and finally of any ruler's house.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是罗马一座山的名字，随后指山上皇帝的宅邸，最后泛指任何君主的宅邸。

senses.title: A bishop's residence
senses.definition: the official residence of a bishop or archbishop, often beside the cathedral
senses.definitionCN: 主教或大主教的官邸，常位于主教座堂旁
senses.example: The archbishop's palace shares a wall with the cathedral garden.
senses.exampleCN: 大主教府与主教座堂的花园共用一道墙。
senses.why: bishops held princely authority in many periods, so their houses took the same word as a king's.
senses.whyCN: 在许多时期主教握有诸侯般的权柄，因此他们的宅邸与国王用同一个词。

senses.title: A very grand private house
senses.definition: a private mansion large and ornate enough to seem royal
senses.definitionCN: 大到与华丽到看上去像王室居所的私人宅邸
senses.example: The merchant built a palace of brick beside the river.
senses.exampleCN: 那位商人在河边建了一座砖砌豪宅。
senses.why: wealth copies the forms of power, so a rich man's house borrows the name of a ruler's house.
senses.whyCN: 财富会模仿权力的形式，因此富人的宅邸借用了君主居所的名字。

senses.title: A public palace of culture
senses.titleCN: 文化宫等大型公共建筑
senses.definition: a large state-built hall for culture, sport or exhibitions, common in former socialist countries
senses.definitionCN: 国家兴建的大型文化、体育或展览场馆，在旧社会主义国家常见
senses.example: The palace of culture has a theatre, a library and a swimming pool.
senses.exampleCN: 这座文化宫里有剧场、图书馆和游泳池。
senses.why: the state took the prestige of the palace and gave it to public leisure, so the word became civic.
senses.whyCN: 国家把宫殿的声望转给公共休闲，因此这个词变得市政化。

senses.title: Any lavish place
senses.definition: a building or room remarkable for comfort, size and expense
senses.definitionCN: 以舒适、宽敞与昂贵著称的建筑或房间
senses.example: The old cinema was a palace of red velvet and gilded plaster.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老电影院是一座红丝绒与镀金灰泥的宫殿。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps only the splendour of the original, dropping the ruler entirely.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻只保留原义的富丽，把君主完全去掉了。

senses.title: The court as a government
senses.definition: the ruler's household and advisers, treated as a political actor
senses.definitionCN: 君主的家臣与顾问群体，被当作一个政治行为者
senses.example: The palace denied that the minister had been dismissed.
senses.exampleCN: 王室方面否认那位大臣已被免职。
senses.why: reporters say 'the palace' when they mean the household that speaks for the ruler.
senses.whyCN: 记者说「王室」时，指的是替君主发声的那套家臣体系。

senses.title: The Palatine hill in Rome
senses.titleCN: 罗马帕拉蒂尼山上的宫殿
senses.definition: the imperial residence on the Palatine hill, whose name became the general word
senses.definitionCN: 帕拉蒂尼山上的皇帝居所，其名字成为通名
senses.example: The ruins of the palace overlook the forum.
senses.exampleCN: 宫殿废墟俯瞰着广场。
senses.why: one hill's name spread until every ruler's house in Europe carried it.
senses.whyCN: 一座山的名字扩散开来，直到欧洲每位君主的宅邸都带上了它。

senses.title: A movie palace
senses.definition: a large, lavishly decorated cinema of the early twentieth century
senses.definitionCN: 二十世纪初那种装饰华丽的大型电影院
senses.example: The movie palace seats two thousand under a painted sky.
senses.exampleCN: 这座电影宫在画出来的天空下可坐两千人。
senses.why: early cinemas sold an evening of luxury, so they named themselves after the most luxurious building they knew.
senses.whyCN: 早期影院卖的是一晚的奢华，因此用他们所知最奢华的建筑来命名自己。

intro.en: Palace is a place name before it is a building word: the Palatine hill in Rome gave its name to the emperor's house and then to grand houses everywhere. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: palace 先是地名，后才是建筑词：罗马的帕拉蒂尼山把名字给了皇帝的宅邸，再给了各地的宏大宅邸。年代均为约数。

items.en: Palatium was the name of one of Rome's seven hills, where Augustus and later emperors built their residences.
items.cn: Palatium 是罗马七座山之一的名字，奥古斯都及后来的皇帝在此营建居所。

items.en: Because the emperor's house stood on that hill, the hill's name became a word for the house itself.
items.cn: 由于皇帝的宅邸立在那座山上，山名便成了指宅邸本身的词。

items.en: Old French palais carried the word into English, where it first named a royal residence.
items.cn: 古法语 palais 把该词带入英语，最初指王室居所。

items.en: In the Middle Ages the word widened to bishops' houses and then to any exceptionally grand town house.
items.cn: 中世纪时该词扩展到主教府，再扩展到任何格外宏大的城中宅邸。

items.en: In the twentieth century states built palaces of culture and workers' clubs, giving the word a public meaning.
items.cn: 二十世纪国家兴建文化宫与工人俱乐部，使这个词带上公共含义。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the origin of the hill name Palatium is disputed; a link to a shepherd god or to a word for a stake has been suggested, but neither is demonstrated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深来源）：山名 Palatium 的来源有争议；有人提出与牧神有关，或与表示「木桩」的词有关，但两者都未得到证实。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like palace or share its grand-house field but differ in origin; group two holds other grand residences.
note.cn: 第一组是与 palace 形近或同属「宏大宅邸」语义场、但来源不同的词；第二组是其他显赫居所。

entries.definition: Like a palace in size and splendour; it describes a quality and never names a building type.
entries.definitionCN: 在体量与富丽上像宫殿；描述一种性质，从不指建筑类型。

entries.definition: The domain of a count palatine, an official with royal powers in a border region; it names land and office.
entries.definitionCN: 宫廷伯爵的领地，指在边境地区拥有王权的官员辖区；指土地与职衔。

entries.definition: An Italian town house of a noble family; English borrowed it for a specific Mediterranean type.
entries.definitionCN: 意大利贵族家族的城中宅邸；英语借来表示一种特定的地中海类型。

entries.definition: A seizure of power by insiders close to the ruler; the phrase uses palace as the seat of power, not as architecture.
entries.definitionCN: 由君主身边内部人发动的夺权；短语把 palace 当作权力中心，而非建筑。

entries.definition: A fortified residence; it stresses defence, while a palace stresses display and administration.
entries.definitionCN: 设防的居所，强调防御；而 palace 强调展示与治理。

entries.definition: A very large private house; it lacks the royal or episcopal rank that palace implies.
entries.definitionCN: 极大型的私人住宅；缺少 palace 所含的王室或主教等级。

entries.definition: The neutral word for an official home, used when rank should not be emphasized.
entries.definitionCN: 指官邸的中性词，用于不宜强调等级时。

entries.definition: A French country house or estate; it combines castle and country house associations.
entries.definitionCN: 法国的乡间宅邸或庄园，兼有城堡与乡居宅邸的联想。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real hill name, the real rank words and the real compounds.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的山名、真实的等级词与真实的复合词。

normal.en: One hill in Rome gave its name to every royal house in Europe.
normal.cn: 罗马的一座山，把名字给了欧洲每一座王室宅邸。

normal.en: The family runs palace, palatial, palatinate, palazzo, palace coup.
normal.cn: 同族说法包括 palace、palatial、palatinate、palazzo、palace coup。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the branches: royal palace, archbishop's palace, palace of culture.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各分支：王宫、大主教府、文化宫。

normal.en: Rank decides the word: a bishop's house and a king's house can both be palaces.
normal.cn: 等级决定用词：主教的宅邸与国王的宅邸都可以叫 palace。

normal.en: The movie palace sold luxury by borrowing the most luxurious name available.
normal.cn: 电影宫借用了当时最奢华的名字来售卖奢华。

abstract.en: Picture a house that has swallowed a whole hill and now wears its name.
abstract.cn: 想象一座房子吞下了整座山，并把山名穿在身上。

abstract.en: Picture a private hallway so long that a guest needs a map to reach the dining room.
abstract.cn: 想象一条私家长廊，长到客人要拿地图才找得到餐厅。

abstract.en: Picture a cinema whose ceiling is painted as a night sky, so the audience sits outdoors indoors.
abstract.cn: 想象一座影院把天花板画成夜空，观众于是在室内坐在户外。

examples.en: The palace was opened as a museum after the monarchy ended.
examples.cn: 君主制结束后，这座王宫被改为博物馆开放。

examples.en: The archbishop's palace dates from the twelfth century.
examples.cn: 大主教府始建于十二世纪。

examples.en: They restored the movie palace instead of demolishing it.
examples.cn: 他们修复了那座电影宫，而没有将其拆除。

dict_mnemonic.text: Palatium（罗马帕拉蒂尼山）→ 山上皇帝宅邸 → 宫殿、豪华宅邸

root: 拉丁 Palatium 原为罗马七丘之一的名字，因皇帝宅邸建于其上而转指宫殿；经古法语 palais 入英语。山名本身的来源不确定。英语 palace。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one address: a ruler's house on a hill becomes a bishop's house, a rich man's house, a public hall, a metaphor, a government, a ruin and a cinema.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个住处展开：山上的君主宅邸成为主教府、富商大宅、公共厅堂、比喻、政府、废墟与影院。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: gate, courtyard, stair and inner hall, each layer admitting fewer people than the last.
core.cn: 核心意象：门、院、阶、内殿，每一层允许进入的人都比前一层更少。

branches.en: THE ORIGINAL HOUSE: the hill name became the emperor's residence, and that residence became the general word.
branches.cn: 最初的宅邸：山名成为皇帝居所之名，那座居所又成为通名。

branches.en: PRINCELY CLERGY: a bishop's house takes the royal word because bishops held princely power.
branches.cn: 诸侯般的主教：主教府沿用王室用词，因为主教握有诸侯般的权力。

branches.en: WEALTH COPIES POWER: a merchant's mansion and a lavish hotel borrow palace's splendour without a ruler.
branches.cn: 财富模仿权力：富商豪宅与豪华旅馆借走了 palace 的富丽，却不要君主。

branches.en: PUBLIC SPLENDOUR: the state builds palaces of culture, and cinemas call themselves movie palaces.
branches.cn: 公共的富丽：国家兴建文化宫，影院则自称电影宫。

branches.en: THE HOUSEHOLD: the building's name moves to the people who speak for the ruler.
branches.cn: 家臣体系：建筑之名转到替君主发声的那群人身上。

intro.en: Palace has no prefix or suffix of its own: it is a place name that became a noun, and its derived words are built on that noun.
intro.cn: palace 本身没有前缀或后缀：它是一个变成名词的地名，其派生词都建在这个名词上。

latinIntro.en: Latin Palatium supplied the name, and the adjective palatinus described what belonged to the imperial hill.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 Palatium 提供了这个名字，形容词 palatinus 描述属于皇帝那座山的事物。

items.exampleCN: 这个名字先指地点，后指建筑。

items.example: The flat has a palatial bathroom.

The palazzo opens onto a small square.
items.exampleCN: 这座府邸朝向一个小广场。

items.meaning: a seizure of power from inside the court
items.meaningCN: 由宫廷内部发动的夺权
items.example: A palace coup removed the old guard.
items.exampleCN: 一场宫廷政变清除了旧班底。

definition_zh: 苍白的；浅色的；逊色的；变苍白
definition_en: having little colour in the face, light and weak in shade, less impressive than something it is compared with, and to lose colour
core_image: 一张血色退去的脸，像被水冲淡的颜色
scene: 清晨的诊室里，医生抬起病人的手腕，看那张几乎没有血色的脸。The nurse noticed how pale his face had become after the long night.
sceneCN: 这里 pale 是「脸色苍白」（第 1 个义项：脸上缺少血色）；句意为护士注意到他熬过漫长一夜之后脸色变得多么苍白。图中可辨识物件：诊室的灯、病人的手腕、床尾的病历夹。

derivatives.zh: pale 加表示性质的后缀 -ness，指苍白、色淡
pale 加副词后缀 -ly，指苍白地、淡淡地
与 pale 同出拉丁语 pallor，指脸色苍白，多用于书面
与 pale 同出拉丁词干 pallidus，指无血色的、病态的苍白

senses.title: Having little colour in the face
senses.definition: having less colour than usual in the face, often because of illness, fear or tiredness
senses.definitionCN: 脸上比平时缺少血色，常因生病、害怕或疲惫
senses.example: She went pale when the results were read out.
senses.exampleCN: 结果念出来的时候，她的脸一下子白了。
senses.why: Latin pallere meant to be pale, and the word has always started from skin losing its healthy colour, so the face is its oldest and most natural subject.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pallere 本义就是发白、失色，这个词最早说的是皮肤失去健康颜色，所以「脸」是它最古老也最自然的落点。

senses.title: Light and weak in shade
senses.definition: of a colour or light, close to white and not strong or deep
senses.definitionCN: 指颜色或光线接近白色，不浓、不深
senses.example: The walls were painted a pale grey.
senses.exampleCN: 墙被刷成了浅浅的灰色。
senses.why: Once the word names a weak version of white, it can describe any colour that has been diluted, which is why pale blue sits nearer white than pure blue.
senses.whyCN: 这个词一旦用来指「被冲淡的白」，就能描述任何掺淡的颜色，所以 pale blue 比纯蓝更靠近白。

senses.title: Weaker than what it is compared with
senses.definition: less impressive, less strong or less real than another thing of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 比同类的另一事物更不打动人、更弱或更不真实
senses.example: The new version is a pale imitation of the old one.
senses.exampleCN: 新版本只是对旧版本一种拙劣的模仿。
senses.why: A pale copy lacks the full colour of the original, so the word came to mean anything that looks washed out beside a stronger model.
senses.whyCN: 淡色的复制品没有原件那样饱满的颜色，于是这个词转指任何在更强的样本旁显得褪色、单薄的东西。

senses.title: To lose colour from the face
senses.definition: to become pale, especially in the face, or to make something seem less strong by comparison
senses.definitionCN: 变得苍白，尤指脸色发白；也可指使某物相形之下显得黯淡
senses.example: His cheeks paled at the sight of the blood.
senses.exampleCN: 一看见血，他的双颊就白了。
senses.why: The verb only sets the adjective in motion: the colour leaves the face while others watch it go, so the change itself becomes the event.
senses.whyCN: 动词只是把形容词动了起来：血色在旁人眼前从脸上退走，于是「退去」这个变化本身成了一件可以叙述的事。

intro.en: Pale comes from Latin pallere, to be pale, through Old French; the same Latin family gives pallor and pallid, so the colour sense is very old.
intro.cn: pale 出自拉丁语 pallere（发白），经古法语进入英语；同一拉丁词族还给出 pallor 与 pallid，颜色义由来已久。

items.en: The verb pallere meant to be pale or to look colourless, and it described the skin before it described anything else.
items.cn: 动词 pallere 意为发白、没有血色，它最初描述的是皮肤，而不是别的物体。

items.en: Its adjective pallidus meant pale or wan and passed into learned words such as pallid.
items.cn: 它的形容词 pallidus 意为苍白、憔悴，后来进入 pallid 这类书面词。

items.en: Old French turned the Latin adjective into pale, and the form crossed to England with Norman French.
items.cn: 古法语把拉丁形容词写成 pale，这个形式随诺曼法语一起进入英格兰。

items.en: Middle English used pale for a face without colour and, by extension, for light and washed-out shades.
items.cn: 中古英语用 pale 指没有血色的脸，并由此延伸到浅淡、发白的颜色。

items.en: Modern English keeps paler and palest as the comparison, and adds the figurative sense of a weak or faded copy.
items.cn: 现代英语用 paler 与 palest 作比较级和最高级，并增加了「逊色、褪色的复制品」这一比喻义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the learned relatives that keep the Latin colour stem; the near-meaning group gathers words for a face or a shade that has lost its strength.
note.cn: 形近组收保留拉丁颜色词干的书面亲属词；近义组收描述失去强度的脸色与色调的词。

entries.definition: Pale and unhealthy, especially of a face; it keeps the Latin adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 苍白而病态的，尤指脸色；保留了拉丁形容词。

entries.definition: The state of being pale, used mostly in medical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 苍白的状态，多用于医学文字。

entries.definition: The quality of being pale; pale plus -ness.
entries.definitionCN: 苍白的性质；pale 加 -ness。

entries.definition: The colour of fresh snow or milk, the lightest shade there is.
entries.definitionCN: 新雪或牛奶的颜色，最浅的色调。

entries.definition: Pale and tired-looking, as if from illness.
entries.definitionCN: 苍白而疲惫的，像病后那样。

entries.definition: Pale grey, like ash, usually of a frightened face.
entries.definitionCN: 灰白的，像灰烬一样，常形容受惊的脸。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a Latin verb for being pale, and everything else in the family returns to a colour that has been drained.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语表示「发白」的动词上，词族里其余的词都回到一种被抽走浓度的颜色。

normal.en: Latin pallere means to be pale, so the word begins at the skin, not at the paint pot.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 pallere 意为发白，所以这个词的起点在皮肤，而不在油漆桶。

normal.en: Pallor and pallid are learned relatives that keep the Latin colour sense.
normal.cn: pallor 与 pallid 是保留拉丁颜色义的书面亲属词。

normal.en: A face goes pale, a colour is pale, and a copy looks pale beside the original: one word measures distance from full colour.
normal.cn: 脸会发白，颜色会发淡，复制品在原件旁显得褪色，同一个词量的是离饱满颜色有多远。

normal.en: The verb pale is simply the adjective set in motion while others watch the colour leave.
normal.cn: 动词 pale 只是把形容词动起来，让别人看着颜色退走。

normal.en: Pale blue is not a kind of blue but blue with white mixed in, which is why the word can also mean weak.
normal.cn: pale blue 不是一种蓝，而是掺了白的蓝，所以这个词也能表示「弱」。

abstract.en: Colour is evidence of health, so losing it is the body's first way of saying that something is wrong.
abstract.cn: 颜色是健康的证据，褪色是身体最先说出「不对劲」的方式。

abstract.en: A pale copy is judged against an original it cannot match, which turns the word into a quiet comparison.
abstract.cn: 淡色的复制品总被拿去和配不上的原件相比，这个词因此成了一场安静的对照。

abstract.en: Every pale thing is a full thing with part of its colour taken away.
abstract.cn: 每个发淡的东西，都是被抽走了一部分颜色的完整之物。

examples.en: She went pale when the results were read out.
examples.cn: 结果念出来的时候，她的脸一下子白了。

examples.en: The walls were painted a pale grey.
examples.cn: 墙被刷成了浅浅的灰色。

examples.en: The sequel is a pale copy of the original film.
examples.cn: 这部续集是原片一个褪色的复制品。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「陪」——病人脸色苍白，床边总得有人陪着；记住 pale 是苍白。

root: 拉丁语 pallere（发白）— pallidus（苍白的）— 古法语 pale — 英语 pale；同族书面词有 pallor、pallid。

sensesIntro.en: The core is colour with its strength taken out; the senses move from the face, to light shades, to the figurative weak copy, and finally to the act of losing colour.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是被抽走浓度的颜色；义项从脸，到浅淡的色彩，再到比喻性的「逊色复制品」，最后回到「失去颜色」这个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a face whose colour has drained away like paint thinned by water.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张血色退去的脸，颜色像被水冲淡的颜料。

branches.en: a patient's face under a clinic lamp
branches.cn: 诊室灯下病人的脸

branches.en: a wall painted a soft grey
branches.cn: 被刷成柔和浅灰的墙

branches.en: a sequel that cannot match the first film
branches.cn: 比不过首部的续集

branches.en: cheeks losing colour at the sight of blood
branches.cn: 见到血时退去血色的脸颊

branches.en: a washed-out colour and a washed-out copy
branches.cn: 褪掉的颜色与褪掉的复制品

intro.en: The word is carried by a Latin verb of being pale, its adjective and noun, and English suffixes that turn the quality into a state or a manner.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语表示发白的动词及其形容词、名词承载，再加上把性质变成状态或方式的英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is well recorded: a verb of being pale, an adjective for the pale colour, and a noun for paleness itself.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族有明确记录：表示发白的动词、指苍白颜色的形容词，以及指苍白本身的名词。

items.meaning: to be pale, to lack colour
